## Objective
- Read TASK.md in full and execute it: extract the complete new-physics content of the SLQrules model (arXiv:2105.04844) into a `spec.json` FeynRulesModel object, run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until schema + lint pass, and finish with a self-audit message.
- Work only inside `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-SLQrules-e1vaqirb/`

## Important Details
- TASK.md rules: `model_name` must be `"SLQrules_gen"`; all numeric physics values are STRINGS (`"-1/3"`, `"1500."`); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups []`; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need no declaration; other indices (colour-sextet, new generation) need `index_decls` (`range_kind "NoUnfold"`, correct size); every particle needs a unique `class_index`; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields.
- COMPLETENESS IS SCORED: all new states (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) as separate ParticleClass entries or `class_members`; include new coupling/mass/mixing params (External unless clearly derived) and main new-physics `lagrangian_terms` as verbatim Mathematica strings using FeynRules idioms.
- Rule 6: read only the paper — never open any cached/reference `.fr` for this model; if one is seen, declare it in the output and don't use it.
- Every new coupling parameter carries `InteractionOrder: {NP, 1}` (overrides paper's own `{QED,2}` on Y13); `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` must declare every order used, e.g. `{{QCD,1},{QED,2},{NP,1}}`.
- Names must not collide with SM.fr declarations (H, Phi, Z, W, A, G, ee, gs, gw, sw, cw, vev, MZ, MW, CKM, ...) or FR/Mathematica builtins (FR_SYMBOLS, PROTECTED sets in fr_lint.py).
- Output must be ONLY the JSON written to `spec.json` via the file-writing tool; final message must be the self-audit (Q/Y/SU2/SU3/charge sums per term, mixing-matrix hermiticity, InteractionOrder/ParameterType sweep, particle/parameter/term counts).
- Bash DENIED except `./frgen` and `./frgen *`; use read/write tools otherwise.
- User directive: "Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed."
- Bash loop rule: run `./frgen spec.json` until schema OK; every remaining lint finding must be checked and judged harmless (recorded in the audit).

- Paper physics (authoritative, re-read this session):
  - 5 scalar LQ reps, all colour fundamental 3: Φ1 (SU2 singlet, Y=-1/3), Φ~1 (singlet, Y=-4/3), Φ2 (doublet, Y=7/6), Φ~2 (doublet, Y=1/6), Φ3 (triplet, Y=-1/3).
  - Charge eigenstates: Φ1^-1/3; Φ~1^-4/3; Φ2=(Φ2^+5/3, Φ2^+2/3); Φ~2=(Φ~2^+2/3, Φ~2^-1/3); σ·Φ3 = [[Φ3^-1/3, √2 Φ3^+2/3],[√2 Φ3^-4/3, -Φ3^-1/3]] ⇒ 9 components (Q=-1/3 ×3, +2/3 ×3, -4/3 ×2, +5/3 ×1).
  - L^LQ = L_2Φ + L_kin + L_f + L_3Φ + L_4Φ; mixing via W matrices (eq:Wmatrices, line 706); mass matrices eq:LQmassMatrices (733); charge vectors eq:ChargeVectors (641); gauge-charge matrices eq:LQchargeMatrices (932); Yukawa eq:LQ_yukawa (1017); C matrix eq:Cmatrix (1035).
  - Covariant derivatives (paper line ~855–867): Φ1: ∂+ (i/3)g1B − g_s λ/2 G; Φ~1: ∂+ (4i/3)g1B − gs λ/2 G; Φ2: ∂−(7i/6)g1B − i g2 σ_I/2 W^I − gs λ/2 G; Φ~2: ∂−(i/6)g1B − i g2 σ/2 W − gs λ/2 G; Φ3: ∂+(i/3)g1B − i g2 ε̃_I W^I − gs λ/2 G.
  - L_kin ⊃ i(e/sw cw) Σ_q (Φ^{q†}ℤ^q ↔∂^μ Φ^q) Z_μ + i(e/sw) Σ_{q≠+5/3} ((Φ^{q+1})† 𝕎_q^{q+1} ↔∂^μ Φ^q) W^+_μ.
  - L_3Φ implementable triple couplings (8): A_1~2~2, A_~12~2, Y_1~12, Y_123, Y_1~23, Y_~123, Y_233, Y_~233.
  - L_f Yukawa families: Y1RR, Y1LL, Y1Q LL (sym), Y1Q RR, Yt1RR, Yt1Q RR (antisym), Y2RL, Y2LR, Yt2RL, Y3LL, Y3Q LL (antisym).
  - L_2Φ params: masses m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3; Y1, Y2, Y3, Yt1, Yt2, Y22, Yt2t2, Y33; dim-1 A1t2, At23; dim-0 Y2t2, Yt13, Y13.
  - Paper's own FR implementation (Methods, lines 1204–1403 = fair game): physical S[100] `S1m13hat` (Q=-1/3, colour triplet, Mass Internal), unphysical S[101] `S1m13` (Y=-1/3, defined via W matrices), also `R2tm13hat`, `S3m13hat`, `W13mat`; param Y13 External, ComplexParameter True, BlockName Y13, Value 1.0, InteractionOrder {QED,2}, Description "S3-S1 scalar leptoquark mixing coupling"; all couplings default to unity.
  - Naming for the 9 mass eigenstates: S1m13hat, S1m43hat, R2p53hat, R2p23hat, R2tm13hat, R2tm23hat, R2tm43hat, S3m13hat, S3p23hat, S3m43hat (per charge assignment above).
  - Unphysical field definition idiom from paper: `S1m13 = HC[W13mat[1,1]] S1m13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[2,1]] R2tm13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[3,1]] S3m13hat[cc]`.
  - FeynRules 2.3.36; GitLab https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules; Table tab:Lagrangians gives FR variable names for L pieces.
- Tooling constraints discovered:
  - `frmodel.py`: `Rule(lhs, rhs, delayed)` → `"lhs -> rhs"` / `":>"`; ParamType External/Internal; External params must be real (complex ⇒ Internal or split real/imag — so paper's complex Y13 can't be External+complex); tensor params use `value_rules`; MassSpec forms: massless | `{sym}` | `{sym, value}` | per-member; unphysical classes require `definitions`; multi-member classes need `flavor_index`; all numerics are strings.
  - `render.py`: Jinja2 skeleton `templates/model.fr.j2` (8 lines: header comment, `M$ModelName = "{{ model_name }}";`, `{{ body }}`); helpers `_bool`, `_quote`, `_strlist`, `_name_field`, `_pdg`; External mass/width params named in Mass/Width specs are dropped from M$Parameters (reserved set `_reserved_mass_width_names`).
  - `fr_lint.py` rules (stage-tagged compile/checks/mg5/harness/warn): rule 10 name checks vs FR_SYMBOLS/PROTECTED/SM names; interaction-order check (every parameter used in a term carries an order, or term uses SM coupling/DC/FS); `_is_kin_name` skips "kin/gauge" terms from order check; no pattern rules (`\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:?->` ⇒ mg5); no explicit flavour sums, no nested generation index (compile), no `DC[Field[...]]` with explicit Colour index (compile); exactly one root total = `LTotal`; every term must contain a field or be a sum of other terms; `SelfConjugate True` ⇒ no nonzero QuantumNumbers; `mixing_in_definitions` (stage checks) fires when Definitions contain ≥2 physical classes AND regex `\b(sa|ca|sin|cos|Sin|Cos|s\w*|c\w*)\w*\b` matches (token `cc` matches `c\w*` ⇒ will fire for colour-indexed W-matrix definitions; judge-as-harmless alternative: no lowercase-s/c token, e.g. colour dummy index named `idx`); undeclared-symbol check where `declared` includes tokens from class Mass/Width specs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read TASK.md fully (including OUTPUT/self-audit instruction).
- Read paper: lines 1–1048, 1049+, 539–1199 (full LQ Lagrangian: reps, L_2Φ, L_kin covariant derivatives + ℤ/𝕎 couplings, L_f, L_3Φ, L_4Φ), 1204–1403 (Methods/GitLab/notebook/Table tab:Lagrangians), 2596–3795, 3796–4995, ~5016–5060, 6410–6477; grep of all 48 `\label{...}` lines with line numbers.

Analysis: unitarity makes unphysical kinetic terms expand to canonical physical ones; free-field mass terms for both bases would double count; lint `mixing_in_definitions` will likely fire for option A (harmless: LQ-LQ self-mixing, not SM mass-basis change).

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

from pydantic import BaseModel, model_validator

# A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
NumberStr = str


class Rule(BaseModel):
    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""

    lhs: str
    rhs: str
    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"

    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"


class ParamType(str, Enum):
    External = "External"
    Internal = "Internal"


class SpinType(str, Enum):
    S = "S"  # scalar
    F = "F"  # fermion
    V = "V"  # vector
    U = "U"  # ghost
    T = "T"  # tensor
    W = "W"  # Weyl fermion
    R = "R"  # spin-3/2
    RW = "RW"


class RangeKind(str, Enum):
    Unfold = "Unfold"
    NoUnfold = "NoUnfold"
    Range = "Range"


class PropType(str, Enum):
    Sine = "Sine"
    Straight = "Straight"
    ScalarDash = "ScalarDash"
    GhostDash = "GhostDash"
    Curly = "Curly"
    W = "W"
    C = "C"
    S = "S"
    D = "D"


class PropArrow(str, Enum):
    true = "True"
    false = "False"
    none = "None"
    forward = "Forward"


class ModelInfo(BaseModel):
    authors: List[str]
    version: str
    date: str
    institutions: List[str] = []
    emails: List[str] = []


class GaugeGroup(BaseModel):
    """A M$GaugeGroups entry. Omitted entirely by BSM add-on models."""

    name: str  # LHS symbol: U1Y, SU2L, SU3C
    abelian: bool
    gauge_boson: str
    coupling_constant: Optional[str] = None
    charge: Optional[str] = None  # required iff abelian
    structure_constant: Optional[str] = None  # required iff non-abelian
    symmetric_tensor: Optional[str] = None
    representations: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # [("T","Colour")] or many
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM rule strings

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "GaugeGroup":
        if self.abelian and not self.charge:
            raise ValueError(f"gauge group {self.name}: Abelian group needs charge")
        if not self.abelian and not self.structure_constant:
            raise ValueError(
                f"gauge group {self.name}: non-Abelian group needs structure_constant"
            )
        return self

    name: str  # Colour, Generation, SU2W ...
    range_kind: RangeKind
    size: int  # Range[size]
    style_symbol: Optional[str] = None  # IndexStyle[name, style_symbol]


class Parameter(BaseModel):
    """A M$Parameters entry (LHS symbol of ``==``)."""

    name: str
    parameter_type: Optional[ParamType] = None
    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # scalar; tensors use value_rules
    value_rules: List[Rule] = []  # tensor Value -> { ... }
    complex: Optional[bool] = None  # ComplexParameter
    block_name: Optional[str] = None  # External only
    order_block: Optional[int] = None  # External SCALAR only
    interaction_order: Optional[Tuple[str, int]] = None  # -> {NP, 1}
    indices: List[str] = []  # non-empty => tensor
    definitions: List[Rule] = []
    parameter_name: Optional[str] = None

    description: Optional[str] = None
    tensor_class: Optional[str] = None

    unitary: Optional[bool] = None
    hermitian: Optional[bool] = None
    orthogonal: Optional[bool] = None
    allow_summation: Optional[bool] = None

    @property
    def is_tensor(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.indices)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "Parameter":

            if self.value is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: tensor uses value_rules, not scalar value"
                )
            if self.order_block is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: order_block forbidden on tensors"
                )
        exclusive = [f for f in (self.unitary, self.hermitian, self.orthogonal) if f]
        if len(exclusive) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: at most one of unitary/hermitian/orthogonal"
            )
        if (self.unitary or self.hermitian) and self.complex is False:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: unitary/hermitian require complex=True"
            )
        if self.orthogonal and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(f"parameter {self.name}: orthogonal must be real")
        if self.parameter_type == ParamType.External and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: External params must be real "
                "(split into real/imag or make Internal)"
            )

    particle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    antiparticle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    full_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_label: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_type: Optional[PropType] = None
    propagator_arrow: Optional[PropArrow] = None

    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM Mathematica rule strings
    ghost: Optional[str] = None  # U[n] only
    goldstone: Optional[str] = None  # S[n] only
    weyl_components: List[str] = []
    majorana_phase: Optional[str] = None
    chirality: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def class_label(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.spin_type.value}[{self.class_index}]"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "ParticleClass":
        if self.unphysical:
            if self.mass or self.pdg:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields omit mass/pdg"
                )
            if not self.definitions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields require definitions"
                )

                    f"particle {self.class_name}: multi-member class needs flavor_index"

                self.particle_name,
                self.antiparticle_name,
                self.full_name,

                        f"member count ({n})"

                    f"particle {self.class_name}: ghosts must be self_conjugate=False"
                )

                raise ValueError(f"particle {self.class_name}: ghost needs ghost=<boson>")
        return self


class LagrangianTerm(BaseModel):
    name: str  # LHS symbol
    expression: str  # VERBATIM Mathematica RHS
    delayed: bool = False  # True -> ":=", False -> "="


def _references(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    """True if ``name`` appears in ``text`` as a whole Mathematica token."""
    if not text:
        return False
    return re.search(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9$]){re.escape(name)}(?![A-Za-z0-9$])", text) is not None

    """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
    texts: List[str] = []
    if p.value:
        texts.append(p.value)
    for r in p.value_rules:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    for r in p.definitions:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    blob = " ".join(texts)
    return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}

    """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.

    Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
    dependency cycle.
    """
    names = {p.name for p in params}
    deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
    by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}

    ordered: List[Parameter] = []
    emitted: set = set()
    remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order

    while remaining:
        progressed = False
        still: List[str] = []
        for n in remaining:
            if deps[n] <= emitted:
                ordered.append(by_name[n])
                emitted.add(n)
                progressed = True
            else:
                still.append(n)
        remaining = still
        if not progressed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"

    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""

        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared

                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"

14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: import os
17: from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
18: 
19: from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape
20: 
21: from .frmodel import (
22:     FeynRulesModel,
23:     GaugeGroup,
24:     IndexDecl,
25:     MassSpec,
26:     Parameter,
27:     ParticleClass,
28: )
29: 
30: _TEMPLATE_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "templates")
31: 
32: 
33: # --------------------------- scalar helpers --------------------------- #
34: 
35: 
36: def _bool(b: bool) -> str:
37:     return "True" if b else "False"
38: 
39: 
40: def _quote(s: str) -> str:
41:     return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
42: 
43: 
44: def _strlist(items: Sequence[str]) -> str:
45:     """M$Information-style: single -> "x"; many -> {"x", "y"}."""
46:     if len(items) == 1:
47:         return _quote(items[0])
48:     return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in items) + "}"
49: 
50: 
51: def _name_field(v) -> str:
52:     """ParticleName/FullName/PropagatorLabel: str -> quoted; list -> {...}."""
53:     if isinstance(v, list):
54:         return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in v) + "}"
55:     return _quote(v)
56: 
57: 
58: def _pdg(v) -> str:
59:     if isinstance(v, list):
60:         return "{" + ", ".join(str(x) for x in v) + "}"
61:     return str(v)
62: 
63: 
64: def _indices(names: Sequence[str]) -> str:
65:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"Index[{n}]" for n in names) + "}"
66: 
67: 
68: # FeynRules QuantumNumbers holds only additive (U(1)-type) charges. Colour/SU2/
69: # etc. are REPRESENTATION labels fixed by a field's Indices, not quantum numbers;
70: # if left in QuantumNumbers, FeynRules emits an unevaluated `Colour[field]` into
71: # the UFO's particles.py, which MadGraph rejects with "name 'Colour' is not
72: # defined". Drop these reserved index/representation names.
73: _REP_LABELS = {
74:     "Colour", "Color", "Sextet", "Gluon", "Generation", "Spin", "Lorentz",
75:     "SU2", "SU2W", "SU2L", "SU2D", "SU2R",
76: }
77: 
78: 
79: def _additive_qns(d: dict) -> dict:
80:     return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k not in _REP_LABELS}
81: 
82: 
83: def _reserved_mass_width_names(particles) -> set:
84:     """Mass/width parameter names FeynRules auto-declares from particle Mass/Width
85:     specs. Declaring them again in M$Parameters double-defines the name in the UFO
86:     (MadGraph InvalidModel), so the renderer drops those duplicates."""
87:     names: set = set()
88:     for p in particles or []:
89:         for spec in (getattr(p, "mass", None), getattr(p, "width", None)):
90:             if spec is None:
91:                 continue
92:             if getattr(spec, "sym", None):
93:                 names.add(spec.sym)
94:             for sub, _val in (getattr(spec, "members", None) or []):
95:                 names.add(sub)
96:     return names
97: 
98: 
99: def _is_internal_param(p) -> bool:
100:     """Internal/derived parameters carry a formula (Definitions) that FeynRules
101:     cannot auto-create from a particle Mass/Width spec, so they must stay in
102:     M$Parameters even when named like a mass/width (e.g. a computed decay width
103:     Width -> {WV1, Internal}). Only plain External duplicates are dropped."""
104:     if getattr(p, "definitions", None):

106:     return "internal" in str(getattr(p, "parameter_type", "")).lower()
107: 
108: 
109: def _qn(d: dict) -> str:
110:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"{k} -> {v}" for k, v in _additive_qns(d).items()) + "}"
111: 
112: 
113: def _interaction_order(t: Tuple[str, int]) -> str:
114:     return f"{{{t[0]}, {t[1]}}}"

116: 
117: def _mw_value(v):
118:     """Normalize a mass/width value. FeynRules' ``Automatic`` width is computed
119:     only when AddDecays is on — which is off for us (broken on Wolfram >=15), so
120:     it leaks the literal ``Automatic`` into the UFO and MadGraph fails with
121:     ``name 'Automatic' is not defined``. Emit a numeric placeholder instead;
122:     MadGraph's compute_widths recovers the real width from the model."""
123:     return "1." if str(v).strip().lower() == "automatic" else v
124: 
125: 
126: def _mass(m: MassSpec) -> str:
127:     if m.massless:
128:         return "0"
129:     if m.members:
130:         parts = [m.sym]
131:         for sub, val in m.members:
132:             val = _mw_value(val)
133:             parts.append(f"{{{sub}, {val}}}" if val is not None else f"{{{sub}}}")
134:         return "{" + ", ".join(parts) + "}"
135:     if m.value is not None:
136:         return f"{{{m.sym}, {_mw_value(m.value)}}}"
137:     return f"{{{m.sym}}}"
138: 
139: 
140: def _reps(reps: Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
141:     if len(reps) == 1:
142:         r, s = reps[0]
143:         return f"{{{r}, {s}}}"
144:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"{{{r}, {s}}}" for r, s in reps) + "}"
145: 
146: 
147: def _assoc(pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]], indent: str = "    ") -> str:
148:     """Render ``{ Key -> val, ... }``, dropping entries whose value is None."""
149:     kept = [(k, v) for k, v in pairs if v is not None]
150:     if not kept:
151:         return "{}"
152:     inner = ",\n".join(f"{indent}{k} -> {v}" for k, v in kept)
153:     close_indent = indent[:-2] if len(indent) >= 2 else ""
154:     return "{\n" + inner + "\n" + close_indent + "}"
155: 
156: 
157: # ------------------------------ blocks ------------------------------- #
158: 
159: 
160: def render_information(info) -> str:
161:     pairs = [
162:         ("Authors", _strlist(info.authors)),
163:         ("Version", _quote(info.version)),
164:         ("Date", _quote(info.date)),
165:         ("Institutions", _strlist(info.institutions) if info.institutions else None),
166:         ("Emails", _strlist(info.emails) if info.emails else None),
167:     ]
168:     return "M$Information = " + _assoc(pairs, indent="  ") + ";"
169: 
170: 
171: def _render_gauge_group(g: GaugeGroup) -> str:
172:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
173:         ("Abelian", _bool(g.abelian)),
174:         ("CouplingConstant", g.coupling_constant),
175:         ("GaugeBoson", g.gauge_boson),
176:         ("Charge", g.charge),
177:         ("StructureConstant", g.structure_constant),
178:         ("Representations", _reps(g.representations) if g.representations else None),
179:         ("SymmetricTensor", g.symmetric_tensor),
180:         (
181:             "Definitions",
182:             ("{" + ", ".join(g.definitions) + "}") if g.definitions else None,
183:         ),
184:     ]
185:     return f"  {g.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
186: 
187: 
188: def render_gauge_groups(groups: List[GaugeGroup]) -> str:
189:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_gauge_group(g) for g in groups)
190:     return "M$GaugeGroups = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
191: 
192: 
193: def render_index_decls(decls: List[IndexDecl]) -> str:
194:     lines: List[str] = []
195:     for d in decls:
196:         if d.range_kind.value == "Range":
197:             rng = f"Range[{d.size}]"

200:         lines.append(f"IndexRange[Index[{d.name}]] = {rng};")

205: 
206: 
207: def _render_parameter(p: Parameter) -> str:
208:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
209:         ("ParameterType", p.parameter_type.value if p.parameter_type else None),
210:     ]
211:     if p.is_tensor:
212:         pairs.append(
213:             (
214:                 "Value",
215:                 ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.value_rules) + "}")
216:                 if p.value_rules
217:                 else None,
218:             )
219:         )
220:         pairs.append(("Indices", _indices(p.indices)))
221:     else:
222:         pairs.append(("Value", p.value))
223:     pairs += [
224:         ("ComplexParameter", _bool(p.complex) if p.complex is not None else None),
225:         ("BlockName", p.block_name),
226:         ("OrderBlock", str(p.order_block) if p.order_block is not None else None),
227:         (
228:             "InteractionOrder",
229:             _interaction_order(p.interaction_order) if p.interaction_order else None,
230:         ),
231:         (
232:             "Definitions",
233:             ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.definitions) + "}")
234:             if p.definitions
235:             else None,
236:         ),
237:         ("ParameterName", p.parameter_name),
238:         ("TensorClass", p.tensor_class),
239:         ("Unitary", _bool(p.unitary) if p.unitary is not None else None),
240:         ("Hermitian", _bool(p.hermitian) if p.hermitian is not None else None),
241:         ("Orthogonal", _bool(p.orthogonal) if p.orthogonal is not None else None),
242:         (
243:             "AllowSummation",
244:             _bool(p.allow_summation) if p.allow_summation is not None else None,
245:         ),
246:         # TeX is a LaTeX label; render it as a quoted Mathematica string with
247:         # backslashes escaped ("\\Gamma_U"), else a raw value like \Gamma_U is a
248:         # Mathematica syntax error that aborts the whole M$Parameters block.
249:         ("TeX", _quote(p.tex) if p.tex else None),
250:         ("Description", _quote(p.description) if p.description else None),
251:     ]
252:     return f"  {p.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
253: 
254: 
255: def render_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> str:
256:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_parameter(p) for p in params)
257:     return "M$Parameters = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
258: 
259: 
260: def _render_particle(p: ParticleClass) -> str:
261:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
262:         ("ClassName", p.class_name),
263:         ("SelfConjugate", _bool(p.self_conjugate)),
264:         (
265:             "ClassMembers",
266:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.class_members) + "}") if p.class_members else None,
267:         ),
268:         ("Indices", _indices(p.indices) if p.indices else None),
269:         ("FlavorIndex", p.flavor_index),
270:         ("Mass", _mass(p.mass) if p.mass else None),
271:         ("Width", _mass(p.width) if p.width else None),
272:         ("QuantumNumbers",
273:          _qn(p.quantum_numbers) if _additive_qns(p.quantum_numbers or {}) else None),
274:         ("PDG", _pdg(p.pdg) if p.pdg is not None else None),
275:         ("ParticleName", _name_field(p.particle_name) if p.particle_name else None),
276:         (
277:             "AntiParticleName",
278:             _name_field(p.antiparticle_name) if p.antiparticle_name else None,
279:         ),
280:         ("FullName", _name_field(p.full_name) if p.full_name else None),
281:         (
282:             "PropagatorLabel",
283:             _name_field(p.propagator_label) if p.propagator_label else None,
284:         ),
285:         ("PropagatorType", p.propagator_type.value if p.propagator_type else None),
286:         ("PropagatorArrow", p.propagator_arrow.value if p.propagator_arrow else None),
287:         ("Ghost", p.ghost),
288:         ("Goldstone", p.goldstone),
289:         ("Chirality", p.chirality),
290:         ("MajoranaPhase", p.majorana_phase),
291:         (
292:             "WeylComponents",
293:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.weyl_components) + "}") if p.weyl_components else None,
294:         ),
295:         ("Unphysical", _bool(True) if p.unphysical else None),
296:         (
297:             "Definitions",
298:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.definitions) + "}") if p.definitions else None,
299:         ),
300:     ]
301:     return f"  {p.class_label} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
302: 
303: 
304: def render_classes(particles: List[ParticleClass]) -> str:
305:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_particle(p) for p in particles)
306:     return "M$ClassesDescription = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
307: 
308: 
309: def render_model(model: FeynRulesModel) -> str:
310:     """Render a validated FeynRulesModel to a complete ``.fr`` string."""
311:     sections: List[str] = [render_information(model.info)]
312: 
313:     if model.interaction_order_hierarchy:
314:         ih = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_hierarchy)
315:         sections.append("M$InteractionOrderHierarchy = {" + ih + "};")
316:     if model.interaction_order_limit:
317:         il = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_limit)
318:         sections.append("M$InteractionOrderLimit = {" + il + "};")
319:     if model.feynman_gauge is not None:
320:         sections.append(f"FeynmanGauge = {_bool(model.feynman_gauge)};")
321:     if model.vevs:
322:         vv = ", ".join(f"{{{f}, {v}}}" for f, v in model.vevs)
323:         sections.append("M$vevs = {" + vv + "};")
324: 
325:     for raw in model.raw_preamble:
326:         sections.append(raw)
327: 
328:     if model.index_decls:
329:         sections.append(render_index_decls(model.index_decls))
330:     if model.gauge_groups:
331:         sections.append(render_gauge_groups(model.gauge_groups))
332:     if model.parameters:
333:         # FeynRules auto-declares the mass/width parameters named in each
334:         # particle's Mass/Width spec. Re-declaring them in M$Parameters makes the
335:         # UFO define the name twice, which MadGraph rejects ("name X define
336:         # multiple time"). Drop those duplicates; keep genuine couplings.
337:         reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)
338:         params = [p for p in model.parameters
339:                   if p.name not in reserved or _is_internal_param(p)]
340:         if params:
341:             sections.append(render_parameters(params))
342:     if model.particles:
343:         sections.append(render_classes(model.particles))
344:     for field, expr in model.gauge_xi:
345:         sections.append(f"GaugeXi[{field}] = {expr};")
346: 
347:     for raw in model.raw_blocks:
348:         sections.append(raw)
349: 
350:     for t in model.lagrangian_terms:
351:         op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
352:         # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
353:         # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
354:         # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
355:         rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
356:         for lead in (":=", "="):
357:             if rhs.startswith(lead):
358:                 rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359:                 break
360:         sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")
361: 
362:     env = Environment(
363:         loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364:         autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),
365:         keep_trailing_newline=True,
366:     )
367:     template = env.get_template("model.fr.j2")
368:     return template.render(model_name=model.model_name, body="\n\n".join(sections))

539: \section{LQ Lagrangian}
540: \label{sec:LQLagrangian}
541: The five possible scalar LQ representations $\Phi_1, \Phi_{\tilde{1}}, \Phi_2, \Phi_{\tilde{2}}, \Phi_3$ transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs} 
542: 
543: 
544: \begin{equation}
545: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
546:     \centering
547:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c}
548:          & $\Phi_1,$ & $\Phi_{\tilde{1}}$ & $\Phi_2$ & $ \Phi_{\tilde{2}}$ & $\Phi_3$\\ \hline
549:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\
550:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 1 & 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\
551:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$ & $-\frac{4}{3}$ & $\frac{7}{6}$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$
552:     \end{tabular}\,.
553: \end{equation}
554: 
555: 
556: Note that we adopt the convention that all scalar LQs transform in the fundamental $SU(3)_c$ representation. Expanding the $SU(2)_L$ multiplets into their components, the following electric charge eigenstates are found
557: 
558: 
559: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
560: \begin{align}
561:     \begin{aligned}
562:         \Phi_1 = \left( \Phi_1^{-1/3}\right), \ 
563:         \Phi_{\tilde{1}} = \left( \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3}\right), \ 
564:         \Phi_2 = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+5/3}_2 \\ \Phi^{+2/3}_2 \end{pmatrix},\ \\
565:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
566:         \Phi_{\tilde{2}} = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\ \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \end{pmatrix},\ 
567:         \sigma \cdot \Phi_{3} = \begin{pmatrix}
568:             \Phi_3^{-1/3} & \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{+2/3} \\
569:             \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{-4/3} & -\Phi_3^{-1/3}
570:         \end{pmatrix}\,. 
571:     \end{aligned}
572: \end{align}
573: 
574: 
575: We decompose the scalar LQ Lagrangian as
576: 
577: 
578: \begin{equation}
579:     \mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}} = \mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}} +
580:     \mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}  + \mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi} \,,
581: \end{equation}
582: 
583: 
584: where $\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$ contains the LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) couplings, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$  the kinetic terms and the couplings to the SM gauge bosons, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}$ the couplings to the SM fermions, $\mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) couplings and finally $\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interaction terms. The individual parts of the Lagrangians are discussed in more detail below. 
585: 
586: 
587: 
588: \subsection{LQ Masses and Higgs Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$)}
589: \label{sec:LQ-Higgs}
590: The LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) interactions are implemented by the Lagrangian \cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy}
591: 
592: 
593: \begin{equation}
594:     \begin{aligned}
595:         \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} 
596:         = &- \sum_{a = 1}^3\big(m_{a}^2+Y_{a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right)\big)\big(\Phi_a^{\dagger}\Phi_a\big)
597:         - \sum_{a = 1}^2 \big(m_{\tilde a}^2+Y_{\tilde a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right) \big)\big(\Phi_{\tilde a}^{\dagger}\Phi_{\tilde a}\big) \\
598: &- Y_{22} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)
599:         - Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big) \\

607: 
608: The color indices are omitted since they just involve trivial contractions. For example, the term with $Y_{22}$ in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) would be $- Y_{22} \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)^\dagger $ $ \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)$ in full notation. We use the convention that couplings with mass dimension one (zero) are denoted by $A$ ($Y$). \\
609: 
610: The terms in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) lead to mixing among the LQ eigenstates of the same electric charge after EW symmetry breaking. It is therefore convenient to collect them in the electric charge eigenstate vectors
611: 
612: 
613: \begin{equation}
614:     \begin{aligned}
615:         \Phi^{-1/3} &\equiv 
616:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
617:                     \begin{pmatrix}
618:                         \Phi_1^{-1/3} \\ 
619:                         \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
620:                         \Phi_3^{-1/3}
621:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, 
622:         &\Phi^{+2/3} &\equiv 
623:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
624:                     \begin{pmatrix}
625:                         \Phi_2^{+2/3} \\ 
626:                         \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
627:                         \Phi_3^{+2/3}
628:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, \\

630:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}

632:                         \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3} \\

635:        &\Phi^{+5/3} &\equiv 
636:        \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
637:                     \begin{pmatrix}
638:                         \Phi_2^{+5/3}
639:                     \end{pmatrix}\,. 
640:     \end{aligned}
641: \label{eq:ChargeVectors}
642: \end{equation}

644: 
645: After spontaneous symmetry breaking, non-diagonal mass matrices $\mathbbm{M}^q$ in
646: 
647: 
648: \begin{equation}
649:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} \supset - \sum_{q \in Q} \Phi^q{}^\dagger \mathbbm{M}^q \Phi^q
650: \end{equation}

652: 
653: are generated with $Q = \left \{ -\frac{4}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \}$ and~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy, AristizabalSierra:2007nf}
654: 
655: 
656: \begin{align}
657:     \begin{aligned}
658:         \mathbbm{M}^{-1/3} &=     \begin{pmatrix}
659:                                     			m_1^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_1 & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}}^*  & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13} \\ 
660:                                     			\frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}} & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
661:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13}^* & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A^*_{\tilde{2}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_3
662:                                 			\end{pmatrix} \,, \\
663:         \mathbbm{M}^{+2/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
664:                                     			m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_2 & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0 \\ 
665:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}}^* & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left( Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \right) & -v A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
666:                                     			0 & - v A_{\tilde{2}3}^* & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_3 + Y_{33} \right)
667:                                 			\end{pmatrix}  \,, \\
668:         \mathbbm{M}^{-4/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
669:                                    			m_{\tilde{1}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{\tilde{1}} & \frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}}Y_{\tilde{1}3}^*\\ 
670:                                     			\frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}} Y_{\tilde{1}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_3 - Y_{33}\right) \\ 
671:                                 			\end{pmatrix}   \,, \\
672:         \mathbbm{M}^{+5/3} &= m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_2 + Y_{22} \right) \,.
673:     \end{aligned}
674: \end{align}
675: 
676: 
677: They can be diagonalized by rotating the LQs with unitary matrices
678: 
679: 
680: \begin{equation}
681:     W^q \Phi^q \equiv \hat{\Phi}^q \,,
682: \end{equation}

684: 
685: in order to arrive at the physical basis with digonal mass matrices. $W^q$ can be calculated perturbatively to arbitrary order in $v$~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Rosiek:2015jua}. At $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ one finds

687: 
688: \begin{align}
689:     \begin{aligned}
690:         W^{-1/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
691:         1\!-\!\frac{v^2|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{4 (m_{1\tilde{2}}^2)^2}& \frac{v A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & \frac{v^2(Y_{13}m_{1 \tilde{2}}^2+A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}A_{\tilde 23})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{1\tilde{2}}^2}\\

693:         \frac{-v A_{\tilde 23}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}\\
694:         \frac{-v^2(Y_{13}^{*}(m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)+A_{1\tilde 2}A_{\tilde 23}^{*})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}&\frac{v A_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}& 1\!-\!\frac{v^2 |A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{4 (m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)^2}
695:         \end{pmatrix}\,,\\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
696: W^{+2/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
697:         1& \frac{v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}}{2 m_{2 \tilde{2}}^2} & 0\\
698:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}^{*}}{2 m_{2\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^{2}|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2} & \frac{-vA_{\tilde 23}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\\
699:         0 & \frac{vA_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2} & 1-\frac{v^2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2 }

706:     \label{eq:Wmatrices}

710: where $m^2_{ab} \equiv m_a^2 - m_b^2$ for $a,b \in \left \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$. 
711: 
712: The diagonal mass matrices 
713: 
714: 
715: \begin{equation}
716:  \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^q \equiv W^q \mathbbm{M}^q \left( W^q \right)^\dagger

719: 
720: then read~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd}

722:

736: 
737: up to order $v^2$. \\
738: 
739: The interactions of LQs with the Higgs field $h$ are determined by

742: \begin{align}
743:     \begin{aligned}
744:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} &\supset \phantom{+} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Gamma}^q \Phi^q \right)h + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{q \in Q}  \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Lambda}^q \Phi^q \right)hh \\

746:     \end{aligned}
747: \end{align}

749:

752: 
753: \begin{equation*}
754: \begin{aligned}
755:            
756:         \mathbb{\Gamma}^{-1/3} &= 
757:                 -v
758:                 \begin{pmatrix}
759:                    Y_1  & \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{13}\\ 
760:                    \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}}{\sqrt{2}v}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{A_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v}\\ 
761:                     Y_{13}^{*} & \frac{A^{*}_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{3}

763:          &\mathbb{\Gamma}^{+2/3} &= 
764:                 \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}

766:                 \begin{pmatrix}

772: \end{equation*}
773: \begin{equation}
774: \begin{aligned}

776:                         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}

part.text:
## Objective
- Read TASK.md and execute it: extract the complete new-physics content of the SLQrules model (arXiv:2105.04844) into a `spec.json` FeynRulesModel object, run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until schema + lint pass, and end with a self-audit message.
- Work only inside `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-SLQrules-e1vaqirb/`

## Important Details
- TASK.md rules: `model_name` must be `"SLQrules_gen"`; all numeric physics values are STRINGS (`"-1/3"`, `"1500."`); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups []`; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need no `index_decls`; other indices need `index_decls` (`range_kind "NoUnfold"`, correct size); every particle needs a unique `class_index`; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields.
- COMPLETENESS IS SCORED: every new state (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) as a separate ParticleClass entry (or `class_members`); new coupling/mass/mixing params (External unless clearly derived); main new-physics `lagrangian_terms` as verbatim Mathematica strings with FeynRules idioms.
- Rule 6: no cached/reference `.fr` for this model may be opened; if seen, declare it in the output. Confirmed by `glob **/*`: only `SM.fr` exists as a `.fr` file (SM.fr is fair game as the SM reference).
- Bash DENIED except `./frgen spec.json` (and `./frgen *`); use read/write tools otherwise. Iterate `./frgen` until schema OK; judge every remaining lint finding as harmless and record it in the audit.
- Every new coupling parameter carries `InteractionOrder: {NP,1}` (overrides paper's `{QED,2}` on Y13); `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` must declare every order used, e.g. `{{QCD,1},{QED,2},{NP,1}}`.
- Names must not collide with SM.fr params/fields (ee, gs, gw, sw, cw, vev, MZ, MW, CKM, Phi, H, Z, W, A, G, cabi, ...) nor FR/Mathematica builtins (FR_SYMBOLS/PROTECTED in fr_lint.py: N, C, D, E, I, K, O, Pi, Gamma, Beta, Zeta, Sqrt, Exp, Log, Sin, Cos, Tan, Re, Im, Conjugate, Sum, Block, Module, Table, If, Which...). Safe new names: m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3, Y1, Yt1, Y2, Yt2, Y3, Y22, Yt2t2, Y33, A1t2, At23, Y2t2, Yt13, Y13, Y1RR, Y1LL, Y1QLL, Y1QRR, Yt1RR, Yt1QRR, Y2RL, Y2LR, Yt2RL, Y3LL, Y3QLL.
- Output: ONLY the JSON written to `spec.json`; final message must be the self-audit (Q/Y/SU2/SU3/charge sums per term, mixing-matrix hermiticity, InteractionOrder/ParameterType sweep, particle/parameter/term counts).
- User directive: "Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed."

### Paper physics (authoritative, re-read this session)
- 5 scalar LQ reps, all SU(3) fundamental 3: Φ1 (SU2 1, Y=-1/3), Φ~1 (SU2 1, Y=-4/3), Φ2 (SU2 2, Y=7/6), Φ~2 (SU2 2, Y=1/6), Φ3 (SU2 3, Y=-1/3) (paper lines 541–572).
- Charge eigenstates: Φ1^-1/3; Φ~1^-4/3; Φ2=(Φ2^+5/3, Φ2^+2/3); Φ~2=(Φ~2^+2/3, Φ~2^-1/3); σ·Φ3 = [[Φ3^-1/3, √2 Φ3^+2/3],[√2 Φ3^-4/3, -Φ3^-1/3]] ⇒ 9 components (Q=-1/3 ×3, +2/3 ×3, -4/3 ×2, +5/3 ×1).
- L^LQ = L_2Φ + L_kin + L_f + L_3Φ + L_4Φ; mixing via W matrices (eq:Wmatrices ~line 706); mass matrices eq:LQmassMatrices (~733): diag entries e.g. m1² + v²/2(Y1 − |A1t2|²/m²_{t̃21}), mt2² + v²/2(Yt2 + |A1t2|²/m²_{t̃21} + |At23|²/m²_{t̃23}), m3² + v²/2(Y3 − |At23|²/m²_{t̃23}), with m²_ab ≡ m_a² − m_b² (lines 725–726).
- Covariant derivatives (~855–867): Φ1: ∂ + (i/3)g1B − gs λ/2 G; Φ~1: ∂ + (4i/3)g1B − gs λ/2 G; Φ2: ∂ − (7i/6)g1B − i g2 σ_I/2 W^I − gs λ/2 G; Φ~2: ∂ − (i/6)g1B − i g2 σ/2 W − gs λ/2 G; Φ3: ∂ + (i/3)g1B − i g2 ε̃_I W^I − gs λ/2 G.
- L_kin ⊃ i(e/sw cw) Σ_q (Φ^{q†}ℤ^q ↔∂^μ Φ^q) Z_μ + i(e/sw) Σ_{q≠+5/3} ((Φ^{q+1})† 𝕎_q^{q+1} ↔∂^μ Φ^q) W^+_μ; ℤ/𝕎 matrices at lines 885–930 (ℤ^{-1/3}, ℤ^{-4/3}, ℤ^{+2/3}, ℤ^{+5/3}; 𝕎^{+2/3}_{-1/3}, 𝕎^{-1/3}_{-4/3}, ...); charge matrices eq:LQchargeMatrices (~932).
- L_2Φ bracket terms (line ~700–730): Y1..Y3, Yt1, Yt2, Y22, Yt2t2, Y33 (dim-4, real), A1t2, At23 (dim-1, complex), Y2t2, Yt13, Y13 (dim-0, complex) + masses m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3.
- L_3Φ implementable triple couplings (8): A_1~2~2, A_~12~2, Y_1~12, Y_123, Y_1~23, Y_~123, Y_233, Y_~233.
- L_f Yukawa families: Y1RR, Y1LL, Y1Q LL (sym), Y1Q RR, Yt1RR, Yt1Q RR (antisym), Y2RL, Y2LR, Yt2RL, Y3LL, Y3Q LL (antisym); Yukawa eq:LQ_yukawa (~1017), C matrix eq:Cmatrix (~1035).
- L_4Φ: only the SM-like quartic Higgs self-coupling structure (lines ~1150–1199).
- Paper's own FR implementation (Methods 1204–1508): physical `S[100]` `S1m13hat` (Q=-1/3, colour triplet, Mass Internal), unphysical `S[101]` `S1m13` (Y=-1/3, defined via W matrices), also `R2tm13hat`, `S3m13hat`, `W13mat`; param Y13 External, ComplexParameter True, BlockName Y13, Value 1.0, InteractionOrder {QED,2}, Description "S3-S1 scalar leptoquark mixing coupling"; all couplings default to unity; Table tab:Lagrangians: LQall, LQ2Phi, LQkin, LQf, LQ3Phi, LQ4Phi; repo https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules.
- 9 mass eigenstate names: S1m13hat, S1m43hat, R2p53hat, R2p23hat, R2tm13hat, R2tm23hat, R2tm43hat, S3m13hat, S3p23hat, S3m43hat (wait: R2tm43hat does not exist — Φ~2 charges are +2/3, -1/3 only; Φ2 gives +5/3,+2/3; Φ3 gives -1/3,+2/3,-4/3 ⇒ 9 total: S1m13hat, S1m43hat, R2p53hat, R2p23hat, R2tm13hat, R2tm23hat, S3m13hat, S3p23hat, S3m43hat).
- Unphysical definition idiom (paper): `S1m13[cc_] :> HC[W13mat[1,1]] S1m13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[2,1]] R2tm13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[3,1]] S3m13hat[cc]`.
- Paper Lagrangian idiom: `L2t33NonHC := Module[{a,b,c,...}, ExpandIndices[ Y2t33 R2t[a,aa] Eps[a,b] 2*Ta[D,b,c] Phi[c] S3[E,bb] I*Eps[D,E,F] S3[F,cc] Eps[aa,bb,cc], FlavorExpand->{SU2D,SU2W}]]; L2t33 := L2t33NonHC + HC[L2t33NonHC];` — index-explicit with `Eps[aa,bb,cc]` colour, `R2t` = Φ~2, `S3` = Φ3, `Phi` = SM Higgs, `R2` = Φ2, `S1` = Φ1, `R1` = Φ~1.

### Tooling / lint facts
- `frmodel.py`: `Rule(lhs, rhs, delayed)` → `"lhs -> rhs"`/`":>"`; ParamType External/Internal; External params must be REAL (complex forbidden — schema raises); tensor params use `value_rules` (masses use `value`); MassSpec forms: massless | `{sym}` | `{sym, value}` | per-member; unphysical classes require `definitions`; multi-member classes need `flavor_index`; all numerics strings.
- `render.py`: Jinja2 skeleton `templates/model.fr.j2`; External mass/width params named in Mass/Width specs are dropped from M$Parameters (reserved `_reserved_mass_width_names`); Internal params are kept.
- `fr_lint.py` rules: rule 10 name checks; interaction-order rule — every param used in a term needs an order (or term uses SM coupling ee/gw/gs/g1/yl/yu/yd/lam/CKM or contains DC/FS[); `_is_kin_name` (names containing "kin"/"gauge") skip the order check; pattern-rule check ⇒ mg5; no explicit flavour sums / nested generation index (compile); no `DC[Field[...]]` with explicit Colour index (compile); exactly one root total = `LTotal`; every term must contain a field or be a sum of other terms; `SelfConjugate True` ⇒ no nonzero QuantumNumbers; `mixing_in_definitions` fires when Definitions reference ≥2 physical classes AND regex `\b(sa|ca|sin|cos|Sin|Cos|s\w*|c\w*)\w*\b` matches the definition text — WORKAROUND DECIDED: name the colour dummy index `aa` (not `cc`) in Definitions so no lowercase s/c token exists ⇒ no finding; term undeclared-symbol check: capital letter followed by `[` or `.` must be in `declared`, which includes tokens from class Mass/Width specs; the `is_mass` computation in rule 11 is unused.

### Design decisions (settled this session)
- Structure: paper-faithful **Design M** — 9 physical mass-eigenstate classes (hat fields, `Mass -> {sym, Internal}`) + 5 unphysical gauge multiplets with W-matrix `definitions` (completeness rule wording "multiplets, mass eigenstates" maps onto these two categories).
- Double-counting rule: free-field mass terms belong to ONE basis; gauge-basis multiplets keep bare masses m1..m3 (External `1500.`) while L_2Φ contributes only Higgs-dependent portal/mixing terms; free-field kinetic terms to be provided for the 9 physical hat fields (physical masses Internal, computed by FR — do NOT declare them in M$Parameters, or declare Internal only if a Value formula is given).
- Parameters: paper's complex couplings (Y13, A1t2, At23, Y2t2, Yt13, Yukawas) cannot be External+complex ⇒ decide between External-real-with-unity-default (task prefers External) vs Internal+ComplexParameter; leaning External, values `"1."`, tensor Yukawas as External with `value_rules` (diagonal unity entries).
- Names for multiplet fields: `S1`, `R1`, `R2`, `R2t`, `S3` (check SM.fr collision: SM `Phi`/`S[3]`/`F[...]` — S1/R1/R2/R2t/S3 are free since SM uses S[1],S[2],S[3] class members not bare symbols... verify).

## Work State
### Completed
- Read TASK.md fully (OUTPUT/self-audit instruction captured).
- Read paper: 1–1048, 1049+, 539–1199 (full LQ Lagrangian), 1209–1508 (Methods, GitLab, Table tab:Lagrangians), 2596–3795, 3796–4995, ~5016–5060, 6410–6477; grep of all 48 `\label{...}` lines.
- Read `tools/frgen/frmodel.py` (schema), `tools/frgen/render.py`, `tools/fr_lint.py` (all rules), `tools/frgen/templates/model.fr.j2`, `SM.fr` 1–569.
- Glob of the whole task dir: only `SM.fr` present as `.fr` (no reference model to avoid).
- Design analysis done: Design M chosen; lint `mixing_in_definitions` workaround (colour dummy `aa`) established; parameter naming list fixed; mass/kinematic bookkeeping rule established.

### Active
- Drafting `spec.json`: particles (9 physical hat classes + 5 unphysical multiplets), parameters (masses, L_2Φ couplings, 11 Yukawa matrices, W-matrix/mixing params), lagrangian_terms for L_2Φ/L_kin/L_f/L_3Φ/L_4Φ + root `LTotal`.

### Blocked
- `frmodel.py` exact JSON field names for `lagrangian_terms` and `index_decls` entries not captured verbatim (both reads truncated) — must re-read the tail before writing spec.json.
- Paper's charge-conjugation appendix (6082–6748) and tail (~6477–end) unread — needed for exact `CC[psi]`/`bar` idioms in L_f terms.

## Next Move
1. Re-read `frmodel.py` tail (verbatim field names for `lagrangian_terms` / `index_decls` / `ParticleClass`) and the paper appendix 6082–6748 + tail for CC idioms.
2. Write `spec.json` (`model_name "SLQrules_gen"`, ~14 particle classes, full parameter set, L_2Φ/L_kin/L_f/L_3Φ/L_4Φ terms, `LTotal` root), then run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate on schema/lint findings until only judged-harmless ones remain.

## Relevant Files

NumberStr = str


class Rule(BaseModel):
    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""

    lhs: str
    rhs: str
    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"

    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"

    Internal = "Internal"

    W = "W"  # Weyl fermion
    R = "R"  # spin-3/2
    RW = "RW"

    Unfold = "Unfold"
    NoUnfold = "NoUnfold"

class PropType(str, Enum):
    Sine = "Sine"
    Straight = "Straight"
    ScalarDash = "ScalarDash"
    GhostDash = "GhostDash"
    Curly = "Curly"
    W = "W"
    C = "C"
    S = "S"

    coupling_constant: Optional[str] = None
    charge: Optional[str] = None  # required iff abelian
    structure_constant: Optional[str] = None  # required iff non-abelian
    symmetric_tensor: Optional[str] = None
    representations: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # [("T","Colour")] or many
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM rule strings

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "GaugeGroup":

    value_rules: List[Rule] = []  # tensor Value -> { ... }
    complex: Optional[bool] = None  # ComplexParameter
    block_name: Optional[str] = None  # External only
    order_block: Optional[int] = None  # External SCALAR only
    interaction_order: Optional[Tuple[str, int]] = None  # -> {NP, 1}

    hermitian: Optional[bool] = None
    orthogonal: Optional[bool] = None
    allow_summation: Optional[bool] = None

    @property
    def is_tensor(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.indices)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "Parameter":

            if self.value is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: tensor uses value_rules, not scalar value"
                )
            if self.order_block is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: order_block forbidden on tensors"
                )
        exclusive = [f for f in (self.unitary, self.hermitian, self.orthogonal) if f]
        if len(exclusive) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: at most one of unitary/hermitian/orthogonal"
            )
        if (self.unitary or self.hermitian) and self.complex is False:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: unitary/hermitian require complex=True"
            )
        if self.orthogonal and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(f"parameter {self.name}: orthogonal must be real")
        if self.parameter_type == ParamType.External and self.complex is True:

    particle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    antiparticle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    full_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_label: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_type: Optional[PropType] = None
    propagator_arrow: Optional[PropArrow] = None

    ghost: Optional[str] = None  # U[n] only
    goldstone: Optional[str] = None  # S[n] only
    weyl_components: List[str] = []
    majorana_phase: Optional[str] = None
    chirality: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def class_label(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.spin_type.value}[{self.class_index}]"

    def _check(self) -> "ParticleClass":

                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields omit mass/pdg"

        texts.append(r.rhs)
    for r in p.definitions:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    blob = " ".join(texts)
    return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}


def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
    """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.

    Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
    dependency cycle.
    """
    names = {p.name for p in params}
    deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
    by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}

    ordered: List[Parameter] = []
    emitted: set = set()
    remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order

    while remaining:
        progressed = False
        still: List[str] = []
        for n in remaining:
            if deps[n] <= emitted:
                ordered.append(by_name[n])
                emitted.add(n)
                progressed = True
            else:
                still.append(n)
        remaining = still
        if not progressed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
            )
    return ordered


class FeynRulesModel(BaseModel):
    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""

    model_name: str
    info: ModelInfo
    interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")

        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
        builtin = {
            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
        }
        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
        return self

539: \section{LQ Lagrangian}
540: \label{sec:LQLagrangian}
541: The five possible scalar LQ representations $\Phi_1, \Phi_{\tilde{1}}, \Phi_2, \Phi_{\tilde{2}}, \Phi_3$ transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs} 
542: 
543: 
544: \begin{equation}
545: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
546:     \centering
547:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c}
548:          & $\Phi_1,$ & $\Phi_{\tilde{1}}$ & $\Phi_2$ & $ \Phi_{\tilde{2}}$ & $\Phi_3$\\ \hline
549:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\
550:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 1 & 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\
551:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$ & $-\frac{4}{3}$ & $\frac{7}{6}$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$
552:     \end{tabular}\,.
553: \end{equation}
554: 
555: 
556: Note that we adopt the convention that all scalar LQs transform in the fundamental $SU(3)_c$ representation. Expanding the $SU(2)_L$ multiplets into their components, the following electric charge eigenstates are found
557: 
558: 
559: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
560: \begin{align}
561:     \begin{aligned}
562:         \Phi_1 = \left( \Phi_1^{-1/3}\right), \ 
563:         \Phi_{\tilde{1}} = \left( \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3}\right), \ 
564:         \Phi_2 = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+5/3}_2 \\ \Phi^{+2/3}_2 \end{pmatrix},\ \\
565:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
566:         \Phi_{\tilde{2}} = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\ \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \end{pmatrix},\ 
567:         \sigma \cdot \Phi_{3} = \begin{pmatrix}
568:             \Phi_3^{-1/3} & \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{+2/3} \\
569:             \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{-4/3} & -\Phi_3^{-1/3}
570:         \end{pmatrix}\,. 
571:     \end{aligned}
572: \end{align}
573: 
574: 
575: We decompose the scalar LQ Lagrangian as
576: 
577: 
578: \begin{equation}
579:     \mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}} = \mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}} +
580:     \mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}  + \mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi} \,,
581: \end{equation}
582: 
583: 
584: where $\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$ contains the LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) couplings, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$  the kinetic terms and the couplings to the SM gauge bosons, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}$ the couplings to the SM fermions, $\mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) couplings and finally $\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interaction terms. The individual parts of the Lagrangians are discussed in more detail below. 
585: 
586: 
587: 
588: \subsection{LQ Masses and Higgs Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$)}
589: \label{sec:LQ-Higgs}
590: The LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) interactions are implemented by the Lagrangian \cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy}
591: 
592: 
593: \begin{equation}
594:     \begin{aligned}
595:         \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} 
596:         = &- \sum_{a = 1}^3\big(m_{a}^2+Y_{a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right)\big)\big(\Phi_a^{\dagger}\Phi_a\big)
597:         - \sum_{a = 1}^2 \big(m_{\tilde a}^2+Y_{\tilde a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right) \big)\big(\Phi_{\tilde a}^{\dagger}\Phi_{\tilde a}\big) \\
598: &- Y_{22} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)
599:         - Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big) \\
600:         &- iY_{33} \epsilon^{IJK} \left(H^\dagger \sigma^I H \right) \Phi_3^{J\dagger} \Phi_3^K\\
601:          \Big[&- A_{1\tilde{2}}\big( \Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger H \big)\Phi_1 + A_{\tilde{2}3}\big(\Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger \left(\sigma \cdot \Phi_3\right) H \big) + Y_{2\tilde{2}}\big(\Phi_{2}^\dagger H \big)\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\Phi_{\tilde{2}}\big)\\
602:         &+Y_{\tilde{1}3}\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3}\right)^\dagger H\big)\Phi_{\tilde{1}} + Y_{13} \big(H^{\dagger}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3} \right)H \big)\Phi_{1}^{\dagger} + \text{h.c.}\Big] \,.
603:     \end{aligned}
604:     \label{eq:LQ_mixing}
605: \end{equation}
606: 
607: 
608: The color indices are omitted since they just involve trivial contractions. For example, the term with $Y_{22}$ in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) would be $- Y_{22} \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)^\dagger $ $ \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)$ in full notation. We use the convention that couplings with mass dimension one (zero) are denoted by $A$ ($Y$). \\
609: 
610: The terms in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) lead to mixing among the LQ eigenstates of the same electric charge after EW symmetry breaking. It is therefore convenient to collect them in the electric charge eigenstate vectors
611: 
612: 
613: \begin{equation}
614:     \begin{aligned}
615:         \Phi^{-1/3} &\equiv 
616:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
617:                     \begin{pmatrix}
618:                         \Phi_1^{-1/3} \\ 
619:                         \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
620:                         \Phi_3^{-1/3}
621:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, 
622:         &\Phi^{+2/3} &\equiv 
623:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
624:                     \begin{pmatrix}
625:                         \Phi_2^{+2/3} \\ 
626:                         \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
627:                         \Phi_3^{+2/3}
628:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, \\
629:         \Phi^{-4/3} &\equiv 
630:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
631:                     \begin{pmatrix}
632:                         \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3} \\ 
633:                         \Phi^{-4/3}_{3}
634:                     \end{pmatrix} \,,
635:        &\Phi^{+5/3} &\equiv 
636:        \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
637:                     \begin{pmatrix}
638:                         \Phi_2^{+5/3}
639:                     \end{pmatrix}\,. 
640:     \end{aligned}
641: \label{eq:ChargeVectors}
642: \end{equation}
643: 
644: 
645: After spontaneous symmetry breaking, non-diagonal mass matrices $\mathbbm{M}^q$ in
646: 
647: 
648: \begin{equation}
649:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} \supset - \sum_{q \in Q} \Phi^q{}^\dagger \mathbbm{M}^q \Phi^q
650: \end{equation} 
651: 
652: 
653: are generated with $Q = \left \{ -\frac{4}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \}$ and~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy, AristizabalSierra:2007nf}
654: 
655: 
656: \begin{align}
657:     \begin{aligned}
658:         \mathbbm{M}^{-1/3} &=     \begin{pmatrix}
659:                                     			m_1^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_1 & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}}^*  & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13} \\ 
660:                                     			\frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}} & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
661:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13}^* & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A^*_{\tilde{2}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_3
662:                                 			\end{pmatrix} \,, \\
663:         \mathbbm{M}^{+2/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
664:                                     			m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_2 & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0 \\ 
665:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}}^* & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left( Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \right) & -v A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
666:                                     			0 & - v A_{\tilde{2}3}^* & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_3 + Y_{33} \right)
667:                                 			\end{pmatrix}  \,, \\
668:         \mathbbm{M}^{-4/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
669:                                    			m_{\tilde{1}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{\tilde{1}} & \frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}}Y_{\tilde{1}3}^*\\ 
670:                                     			\frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}} Y_{\tilde{1}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_3 - Y_{33}\right) \\ 
671:                                 			\end{pmatrix}   \,, \\
672:         \mathbbm{M}^{+5/3} &= m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_2 + Y_{22} \right) \,.
673:     \end{aligned}
674: \end{align}
675: 
676: 
677: They can be diagonalized by rotating the LQs with unitary matrices
678: 
679: 
680: \begin{equation}
681:     W^q \Phi^q \equiv \hat{\Phi}^q \,,
682: \end{equation}
683: 
684: 
685: in order to arrive at the physical basis with digonal mass matrices. $W^q$ can be calculated perturbatively to arbitrary order in $v$~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Rosiek:2015jua}. At $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ one finds
686: 
687: 
688: \begin{align}
689:     \begin{aligned}
690:         W^{-1/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
691:         1\!-\!\frac{v^2|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{4 (m_{1\tilde{2}}^2)^2}& \frac{v A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & \frac{v^2(Y_{13}m_{1 \tilde{2}}^2+A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}A_{\tilde 23})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{1\tilde{2}}^2}\\
692:         \frac{-v A_{1\tilde 2}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^2}{4}\left(\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{(m_{1\tilde{2}}^2 )^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{(m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2)^2}\!\right)&
693:         \frac{-v A_{\tilde 23}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}\\
694:         \frac{-v^2(Y_{13}^{*}(m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)+A_{1\tilde 2}A_{\tilde 23}^{*})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}&\frac{v A_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}& 1\!-\!\frac{v^2 |A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{4 (m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)^2}
695:         \end{pmatrix}\,,\\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
696: W^{+2/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
697:         1& \frac{v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}}{2 m_{2 \tilde{2}}^2} & 0\\
698:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}^{*}}{2 m_{2\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^{2}|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2} & \frac{-vA_{\tilde 23}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\\
699:         0 & \frac{vA_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2} & 1-\frac{v^2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2 }
700:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \,W^{-4/3}\approx\begin{pmatrix}
701:         1 & \frac{v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}\\
702:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}}{\sqrt{2} m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}& 1
703:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \\
704: W^{+5/3} &= 1 \,,
705:     \end{aligned}
706:     \label{eq:Wmatrices}
707: \end{align}
708: 
709: 
710: where $m^2_{ab} \equiv m_a^2 - m_b^2$ for $a,b \in \left \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$. 
711: 
712: The diagonal mass matrices 
713: 
714: 
715: \begin{equation}
716:  \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^q \equiv W^q \mathbbm{M}^q \left( W^q \right)^\dagger 
717: \end{equation}
718: 
719: 
720: then read~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd}
721: 
722: 
723: \begin{equation}
724: \begin{aligned}
725: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{-1/3}&\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(m_{1}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{1}\!-\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}1}^2}\!\right) , \, m_{\tilde{2}}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{\tilde{2}}\!+\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}1}^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\!\right),\, \\ 
726:  & \phantom{\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(\,} m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{3}\!-\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\right)\Bigg)\,, \\
727: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{+2/3} &\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(m_{2}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}Y_{2} , \, m_{\tilde{2}}^2 +\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(Y_{\tilde{2}}+\!Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}}\!+\!\frac{2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\! \right),\, \\ 
728:  & \phantom{\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(\,} m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{3} + Y_{33} \!-\!\frac{2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\!\right)
729: \Bigg)\,, \\
730: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{-4/3}&\approx \text{diag}\left(m_{\tilde{1}}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}Y_{\tilde{1}}, \, m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(Y_{3} - Y_{33}\right)\right)\,, \\
731: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{+5/3}&=m_{2}^2+\frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_{2}+Y_{22}\right)\,,
732: \end{aligned}
733: \label{eq:LQmassMatrices}
734: \end{equation}
735: 
736: 
737: up to order $v^2$. \\
738: 
739: The interactions of LQs with the Higgs field $h$ are determined by
740: 
741: 
742: \begin{align}
743:     \begin{aligned}
744:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} &\supset \phantom{+} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Gamma}^q \Phi^q \right)h + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{q \in Q}  \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Lambda}^q \Phi^q \right)hh \\
745:     & = \phantom{+} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \hat{\Phi}^{q\dagger} \hat{\mathbb{\Gamma}}^q \hat{\Phi}^q \right)h + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \hat{\Phi}^{q\dagger} \hat{\mathbb{\Lambda}}^q \hat{\Phi}^q \right)hh \,, \\
746:     \end{aligned}
747: \end{align}
748: 
749: 
750: with
751: 
752: 
753: \begin{equation*}
754: \begin{aligned}
755:            
756:         \mathbb{\Gamma}^{-1/3} &= 
757:                 -v
758:                 \begin{pmatrix}
759:                    Y_1  & \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{13}\\ 
760:                    \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}}{\sqrt{2}v}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{A_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v}\\ 
761:                     Y_{13}^{*} & \frac{A^{*}_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{3}
762:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, 
763:          &\mathbb{\Gamma}^{+2/3} &= 
764:                 \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
765:                 -v
766:                 \begin{pmatrix}
767:                    Y_2  & Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
768:                   Y^{*}_{2\tilde{2}}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde2 \tilde2} & -\frac{A_{23}}{v}\\ 
769:                     0 & -\frac{A^{*}_{23}}{v} & Y_3 + Y_{33}
770:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, \\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
771: \end{aligned}
772: \end{equation*}
773: \begin{equation}
774: \begin{aligned}
775:         \mathbb{\Gamma}^{-4/3} &= 
776:                         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
777:                         -v
778:                         \begin{pmatrix}
779:                           Y_{\tilde{1}}  & \sqrt{2} Y^{*}_{\tilde{1}3} \\ 
780:                           \sqrt{2} Y_{\tilde{1}3}  & Y_3 - Y_{33} \\
781:                         \end{pmatrix}\,, 
782:         &\mathbb{\Gamma}^{+5/3} &= -v \Big(Y_2 + Y_{22} \Big) \,, \\
783:         \mathbb{\Lambda}^{-1/3} &= 
784:                 -\phantom{v}\begin{pmatrix}
785:                    Y_1  & 0 & Y_{13}\\ 
786:                    0  & Y_{\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
787:                     Y_{13}^{*} & 0 & Y_3
788:                 \end{pmatrix} \,,
789:         &\mathbb{\Lambda}^{+2/3} &=
790:                 -\phantom{v} \begin{pmatrix}
791:                    Y_2 & Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
792:                   Y^{*}_{2\tilde{2}}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde2 \tilde2} & 0\\ 
793:                     0 & 0 & Y_3 + Y_{33}
794:                 \end{pmatrix} \,, \\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
795:         \mathbb{\Lambda}^{-4/3} &=
796:                 -\phantom{v}\begin{pmatrix}
797:                    Y_{\tilde{1}}  & \sqrt{2} Y^{*}_{\tilde{1}3} \\ 
798:                   \sqrt{2} Y_{\tilde{1}3}  & Y_3 - Y_{33} \\
799:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, 
800:         &\mathbb{\Lambda}^{+5/3} &= -\phantom{v}\Big(Y_2 + Y_{22}\Big)\,, \\
801:     \end{aligned}
802: \end{equation}
803: 
804: 
805: and
806: 
807: 
808: \begin{align}
809: 	\begin{aligned}
810: 		\hat{\mathbb{\Gamma}}^q &= W^q \mathbb{\Gamma}^q \left(W^{q}\right)^\dagger \text{ for } q \in Q \,, \\
811: 		\hat{\mathbb{\Lambda}}^q &= W^q \mathbb{\Lambda}^q \left(W^{q}\right)^\dagger \text{ for } q \in Q \,.
812: 	\end{aligned}
813: \end{align} \\
814: 
815: 
816: The explicit expressions for these coupling matrices up to $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ are given in Ref.~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd}. \\
817: 
818: When listing the Feynman rules for interactions involving LQs of the same charge, we will have to relate the LQ label $a \in \left \{ 1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$ to the position in $\Phi^q$. For this we use the coefficients
819: 
820: 
821: \begin{equation}
822:     n_a^q \text{ with } q \in \left \{-\frac{4}{3},-\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \} \text{ and } a \in \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \}.
823:     \label{eq:nqi}
824: \end{equation}
825: 
826: 
827: Explicitly, we have
828: 
829: 
830: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
831: \begin{center}
832:     \begin{tabular}{ r|c c c c c c|}
833:      $n_a^q$ & $a = 1$ & $a = \tilde{1}$ & $a = 2$ & $a = \tilde{2}$ & $a = 3$ \\
834:     \hline
835:        $q = -\frac{1}{3}$ & 1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\
836:        $q = +\frac{2}{3}$ & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
837:        $q = -\frac{4}{3}$ & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\
838:        $q = +\frac{5}{3}$ & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\
839:     \end{tabular}\,.
840: \end{center}
841: 
842: 
843: Whenever $q$ is clear from the context, we write $n^q_a$ as $n_a$ to simplify the notation. 
844: 
845: 
846: 
847: \subsection{Kinetic Terms and Interactions with SM Gauge Bosons ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$)}
848: \label{sec:LQkin}
849: The kinetic terms for the LQs as well as their couplings to the SM gauge bosons are presented in this section. The same conventions as for the SM are used. For the three-dimensional adjoint representation of $SU(2)_L$, the $I^{\text{th}}$ generator ($I \in \{1,2,3\}$) has the $3\times3$ matrix form  $(\tilde{\epsilon}_I)_{JK} \equiv i \epsilon_{IJK}$, where $\epsilon_{IJK}$ is the three-dimensional Levi-Civita tensor.  We use the convention $\epsilon_{123} = +1$.
850: 
851: 
852: \begin{equation}
853:     \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
