display.text:
You are benchmarking automated extraction of a BSM physics model from its paper, to be compared against the physicist's own FeynRules implementation.

MODEL: SLQrules (SimpleExtensions) — FeynRules DB entry based on arXiv:2105.04844.
PAPER: the paper's LaTeX source is the file "paper/2105.04844_source.tex" (read it completely with your file-reading tool; equations, fractions and roots are exact; it is authoritative).
SCHEMA: read tools/frgen/frmodel.py (pydantic FeynRulesModel) before you write the spec.

TASK — extract the COMPLETE new-physics content:
1. Read the paper. Identify EVERY new particle beyond the Standard Model: spin (S/F/V), colour rep (singlet/triplet/sextet/octet), SU(2) rep, electric charge Q and/or hypercharge Y, mass parameter. COMPLETENESS IS SCORED — a model with several new states (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) must include all of them as separate ParticleClass entries (or class_members).
2. Identify the new coupling/mass/mixing parameters (External unless clearly derived).
3. Include the main new-physics lagrangian_terms (verbatim Mathematica strings, FeynRules idioms).

SCHEMA RULES: all numeric physics values are STRINGS ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on => gauge_groups []; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need NO declaration; any OTHER index (e.g. a colour-sextet index, a new-generation index) NEEDS an index_decls entry (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); every particle needs a unique class_index; self_conjugate=false for complex fields (distinct antiparticle), true for real/Majorana fields.

OUTPUT: write the FeynRulesModel JSON object to spec.json in the current directory with your file-writing tool (ONLY the JSON). Set model_name to "SLQrules_gen". Run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate as described under TOOLKIT. Your final message: the self-audit table and one line with the last ./frgen result. spec.json as it is on disk when you stop is rendered and scored.

SANDBOX: the current directory contains ONLY the paper (paper/2105.04844_source.tex), SM.fr (the Standard
Model file this add-on is loaded on top of: take field names, index conventions and
hypercharges from it), the schema tools/frgen/frmodel.py, the renderer
tools/frgen/render.py, the lints tools/fr_lint.py and the command ./frgen. Nothing else
exists here and nothing outside this directory may be read. You have file read, search and
write tools, and ONE shell command: `./frgen spec.json`. No other shell command, no web,
no FeynRules, no Mathematica and no MadGraph.

TOOLKIT: `./frgen spec.json` (1) validates spec.json against the FeynRulesModel schema and
prints every schema error, (2) renders model.fr with the deterministic renderer, and (3)
lints model.fr with deterministic rules, each tagged with the stage it predicts will fail.
Run it after you write spec.json, fix what it reports, and run it again until the schema
is OK and every remaining lint finding is one you have checked and judged harmless.

## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
   - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
   - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
   - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.

4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.

5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
   - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.
   - Otherwise cross-check the placement against a second equation of the paper that depends on the same coefficient (a partial width, a cross section, a limit, or a small-parameter expansion) and name that equation in the self-audit. A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
   - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.
   Never silently pick one placement.

8. Mass mixing. When the paper diagonalises a mass mixing between a new state and an SM state (Z-Z', h-S, W-W_R, nu-N), write the mass eigenstates the paper uses: declare the mixing angle (External, or Internal with the paper's formula) and express the gauge eigenstates through it in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes. Do not leave the mixing in a comment.

## FeynRules and UFO construct rules (each one broke a compile or a MadGraph import in earlier runs)

9. Non-fundamental colour representations. If a field carries a colour index other than the triplet `Colour` or the adjoint `Gluon` (for example a sextet), declare the index range AND add the representation line FeynRules needs, before the field declarations: `AddGaugeRepresentation[SU3C -> {T6, Sextet}];` for a sextet (schema: put both lines in `raw_preamble`; also keep the `index_decls` entry). Write covariant derivatives on the whole field, `DC[Phi, mu]`, never with an explicit colour index inside `DC[...]`.

10. Names. Class names, parameter names and index names must not be Mathematica built-ins or FeynRules symbols: never `N`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `I`, `K`, `O`, `HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, and never a name SM.fr already declares (`H`, `Phi`, `Z`, `W`, `A`, `G`, `ee`, `gs`, `gw`, `sw`, `cw`, `vev`, `MZ`, `MW`, ...). No primes or punctuation in `ParticleName`/`AntiParticleName` (`W'` is not a valid UFO name; write `Wp`, `Wpbar`). Use class indices of 100 or more for new classes.

11. Interaction orders. Every new coupling parameter (Yukawa, portal, quartic, new gauge coupling, dimensionless EFT coefficient) carries an `InteractionOrder`: `{NP, 1}` for a new-physics coupling, `{QED, 1}` or `{QCD, 1}` only when it is literally that coupling. Declare `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` with every order you use (for example `{{QCD, 1}, {QED, 2}, {NP, 1}}`). A coupling with no order makes MadGraph reject the UFO ("Some couplings have '1' order").

12. Tensor parameters. Give every indexed parameter explicit per-component values (`yN[1,1] -> 0.1, yN[1,2] -> 0, ...`; schema: `value_rules`). Never use a pattern rule such as `X[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> ...` in `Definitions`: FeynRules exports the pattern verbatim as a UFO parameter name and MadGraph fails with an unrelated "invalid syntax" error.

13. Flavour structure in matrix form. Write generation-space couplings as matrix products between class fields, `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `LLbar.yN.NR`, `ISbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.IS`, not as explicit index sums `VCKMR[ff1, ff2] uqbar[ff1, cc]...dq[ff2, cc]`, and never nest one generation index inside another. Explicit-index forms leak FeynRules internals (`ConvertSpinToString`, `MakeIdenticalFermions`) into the UFO.

14. One declared total. Define exactly one Lagrangian term named `LTotal` that sums every other term you define, and make sure every other term appears in that sum. Do not define two alternative totals. Do not emit a term that contains no field (a pure constant): FeynRules exports it as a vertex with no particles.

15. Declarations. Every field used in a term is declared; every parameter used in a term is declared with a numeric default; every `SelfConjugate -> True` class has no `QuantumNumbers`; a Majorana mass term is `-1/2 M psibar.psi`.

## Mandatory self-audit table (produce it BEFORE the model)

For every Lagrangian term you emit, output one row of this table. Then fix any row that fails before you write the model.

| term name | fields in the monomial | operator mass dimension d | coupling symbol | coupling mass dimension (must be 4 - d) | 1/Lambda power present (must be d - 4, or "n/a" if d <= 4) | Q sum | Y sum | SU(2) contraction (singlet? which Eps or shared index) | SU(3) contraction | sum of each new U(1) charge (one column per U(1), must be 0) | lepton/baryon number sum (if the paper assigns them) | CC[] used where paper writes psi^c (yes/no/n/a) | fraction/root placement checked against (equation, LaTeX line, or "n/a") | Hermitian partner (HC[] or self-conjugate) |

Rules for the table:
- Field mass dimensions: scalar 1, vector 1, fermion 3/2, `FS[...]` 2, `del`/`DC` 1.
- Every Q sum, Y sum, and new-U(1) sum must equal 0. Use the charges you declared in `QuantumNumbers` and the SM.fr charges for SM fields. If a sum is not 0, the term is wrong; fix the contraction or the charge before you continue.
- If d > 4, the row must show `1/Lambda^(d-4)` and an External cutoff parameter, or a Description that states the absorbed dimension and units.
- Add one row per new particle class that confirms its kinetic + mass term exists and is in the total Lagrangian sum.
- Add one row per non-fundamental colour representation that confirms the `AddGaugeRepresentation[...]` line is present.
- Add one line under the table that lists every `SelfConjugate -> True` class and confirms it carries no `QuantumNumbers`.
- Add one line that lists every class, parameter and index name you chose and confirms none is a Mathematica built-in, a FeynRules symbol, or an SM.fr name.
- Add one line that names the single total Lagrangian and lists the terms it sums.
- Add one line that states whether any reference or cached model file was read (must be "none").

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.
3: 
4: Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
5: MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
6: repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
7: predicts takes up to 900 s.
8: 
9: Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import json
22: import re
23: import sys
24: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
25: from pathlib import Path
26: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
27: 
28: HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
29: SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"
30: 
31: # Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}
39: 
40: # Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
42: SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
43: SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
44: for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
45:     SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
46: _i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
47: SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
48: SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
49: SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
50:               "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
51: SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
52: SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
53:              "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}
54: 
55: FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
56:                "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
57:                "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
58:                "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
59:                "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
60:                "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
61:                "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
62:                "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
63:                "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
64:                "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}
65:

67: @dataclass
68: class Finding:
69:     rule: str
70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None
73: 
74: 
75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1
109: 
110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None
157: 
158: 
159: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- lints
160: 
161: def lint_text(raw: str) -> List[Finding]:
162:     text = strip_comments(raw)
163:     F: List[Finding] = []
164:     classes = _entries(_block(text, "ClassesDescription"))
165:     params = _entries(_block(text, "Parameters"))
166:     terms = term_defs(text)
167:     term_names = {t["name"] for t in terms}
168:     term_bodies = "\n".join(t["body"] for t in terms)
169: 
170:     class_names, class_idx = {}, {}
171:     for c in classes:
172:         cn = _prop(c["body"], "ClassName")
173:         if cn:
174:             class_names[cn] = c
175:             mi = re.match(r"(\w+)\[\s*(\d+)\s*\]", c["head"])
176:             if mi:
177:                 class_idx[cn] = (mi.group(1), int(mi.group(2)))
178:     param_names = {p["head"]: p for p in params}
179:     index_decls = dict(re.findall(r"IndexRange\[\s*Index\[(\w+)\]\s*\]\s*=\s*([^;\n]+)", text))
180: 
181:     # --- rule 10: names -------------------------------------------------
182:     for name in list(class_names) + list(param_names) + list(index_decls):
183:         if name in FR_SYMBOLS:
184:             F.append(Finding("feynrules_symbol_name", "compile",
185:                              f"`{name}` is a FeynRules symbol", _line_of(text, name)))
186:         elif name in PROTECTED:
187:             F.append(Finding("protected_name", "warn",
188:                              f"`{name}` is a Mathematica built-in (loads with a warning; renaming is safer)",
189:                              _line_of(text, name)))
190:     for name in class_names:
191:         if name in SM_CLASSES or name in SM_MEMBERS:
192:             F.append(Finding("sm_class_redeclared", "warn",
193:                              f"class `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr (doubly-defined class)",
194:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {name}")))
195:     for name in param_names:
196:         if name in SM_PARAMS or name in SM_MASSES:
197:             F.append(Finding("sm_parameter_redeclared", "warn",
198:                              f"parameter `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr", _line_of(text, name)))
199:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
200:         for key in ("ParticleName", "AntiParticleName"):
201:             v = _prop(c["body"], key)
202:             names = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', v) if v else []
203:             if v and any(re.search(r"[\'`\s!@#%^&*()=\[\]{}|\\;:<>?/,]", nm) for nm in names):
204:                 F.append(Finding("bad_particle_name", "mg5",
205:                                  f"class `{cn}`: {key} {v} is not a valid UFO identifier", _line_of(text, v)))
206:         if cn in class_idx and class_idx[cn][1] < 100:
207:             F.append(Finding("low_class_index", "warn",
208:                              f"class `{cn}` uses index {class_idx[cn][0]}[{class_idx[cn][1]}]; SM.fr uses the low indices",
209:                              _line_of(text, c["head"])))
210:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
211:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
212:                 if mem in SM_MEMBERS or mem in SM_CLASSES:
213:                     F.append(Finding("sm_member_redeclared", "compile",
214:                                      f"class member `{mem}` of `{cn}` collides with an SM.fr name",
215:                                      _line_of(text, mem)))
216:     if "$" in re.sub(r"M\$\w+", "", text):
217:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b\w*\$\w*", text):
218:             if not re.match(r"^(M|MR|FR)\$", m.group(0)):
219:                 F.append(Finding("dollar_in_name", "mg5", f"`{m.group(0)}` contains `$` (invalid Python)",
220:                                  text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1))
221:                 break
222: 
223:     # --- rule 11: interaction orders --------------------------------------
224:     hierarchy = _block(text, "InteractionOrderHierarchy")
225:     orders_declared = set(re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*-?\d+\s*\}", hierarchy))
226:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
227:         body = p["body"]
228:         ptype = (_prop(body, "ParameterType") or "External").strip()
229:         io = _prop(body, "InteractionOrder")
230:         used = re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", term_bodies) is not None
231:         is_mass = any(re.search(rf"Mass\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"]) or
232:                       re.search(rf"Width\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"])
233:                       for c in classes) or re.match(r"^(M|W)[A-Z]", pn) and not io
234:         if io:
235:             oname = re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,", io)
236:             for o in oname:
237:                 if o not in orders_declared and o not in ("QCD", "QED"):
238:                     F.append(Finding("order_not_in_hierarchy", "warn",
239:                                      f"parameter `{pn}` uses InteractionOrder `{o}` not listed in M$InteractionOrderHierarchy",
240:                                      _line_of(text, pn)))
241:     ordered = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items() if _prop(p["body"], "InteractionOrder")}
242:     internal = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items()
243:                 if (_prop(p["body"], "ParameterType") or "External").strip() == "Internal"}
244:     # an Internal parameter inherits the orders of the parameters in its Value
245:     for pn in list(internal):
246:         val = _prop(param_names[pn]["body"], "Value") or ""
247:         if any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(o)}\b", val) for o in ordered):
248:             ordered.add(pn)
249:     for t in terms:
250:         if _is_kin_name(t["name"]):
251:             continue
252:         used_params = {pn for pn in param_names if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", t["body"])}
253:         sm_couplings = {"ee", "gw", "gs", "g1", "yl", "yu", "yd", "lam", "CKM"}
254:         if used_params and not (used_params & ordered) and not \
255:                 any(re.search(rf"\b{c}\b", t["body"]) for c in sm_couplings) and \
256:                 not any(re.search(rf"\b(DC|FS)\[", t["body"]) for _ in [0]):
257:             F.append(Finding("missing_interaction_order", "mg5",
258:                              f"`{t['name']}`: none of its parameters ({', '.join(sorted(used_params))}) carries an InteractionOrder",
259:                              t["line"]))
260: 
261:     # --- rule 12: pattern rules on tensor parameters -----------------------
262:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
263:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:?->", p["body"]) or "_?NumericQ" in p["body"]:
264:             F.append(Finding("pattern_rule_definition", "mg5",
265:                              f"parameter `{pn}` uses a pattern rule in Definitions/Value; FeynRules exports it verbatim as a UFO name",
266:                              _line_of(text, pn)))
267:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
268:         d = _prop(c["body"], "Definitions") or ""
269:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:>", d) and not re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_\s*[,\]]", d):
270:             pass  # `X[mu_] :> ...` is the normal FeynRules idiom; leave it
271: 
272:     # --- rule 13: explicit indices ------------------------------------------
273:     for t in terms:
274:         b = t["body"]
275:         for m in re.finditer(r"DC\[\s*(\w+)\[([^\]]*)\]\s*,", b):
276:             fld = m.group(1)
277:             c = class_names.get(fld)
278:             idx = (_prop(c["body"], "Indices") or "") if c else ""
279:             if c and re.search(r"Colour|Sextet|Gluon|Octet|Col", idx):
280:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "compile",
281:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on `{fld}` with an explicit colour-type index", t["line"]))
282:             else:
283:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "warn",
284:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on an explicitly indexed field `{fld}`", t["line"]))
285:             break
286:         if re.search(r"Index\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]\s*,\s*Index\[\s*Generation", b) or \
287:                 re.search(r"\w+\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]", b):
288:             F.append(Finding("nested_generation_index", "compile",
289:                              f"`{t['name']}`: nested generation index", t["line"]))
290:         m = re.search(r"\b(\w+)\[\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|ii\d?)\s*,\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|jj\d?)\s*\]\s*\w+bar\[", b)
291:         if m and m.group(1) in param_names:
292:             F.append(Finding("explicit_flavour_sum", "mg5",
293:                              f"`{t['name']}`: flavour matrix `{m.group(1)}` with explicit generation indices instead of matrix form",
294:                              t["line"]))
295: 
296:     # --- rule 14: one declared total ---------------------------------------
297:     roots = []
298:     for t in terms:
299:         if not any(re.search(rf"\b{t['name']}\b", u["body"]) for u in terms if u is not t):
300:             roots.append(t["name"])
301:     if terms and not roots:
302:         F.append(Finding("no_total_lagrangian", "harness", "no Lagrangian symbol is a root (circular or empty)", None))
303:     elif len(roots) > 1:
304:         F.append(Finding("ambiguous_total", "harness",
305:                          f"{len(roots)} root Lagrangian symbols: {', '.join(roots)}", None))
306:     elif roots and roots[0] not in ("LTotal", "LTot", "LFull", "LBSM", "LNP", "Lag", "LagTot"):
307:         F.append(Finding("total_not_named_ltotal", "warn", f"the single root is `{roots[0]}`, not LTotal", None))
308:     field_tokens = set(class_names) | {c + "bar" for c in class_names} | SM_FIELDS_ALL
309:     for c in classes:
310:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
311:             field_tokens |= {x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()}
312:     for t in terms:
313:         rhs = t["body"].split("=", 1)[-1]
314:         if re.search(r"\bL\w+\b", rhs) and any(re.search(rf"\b{u['name']}\b", rhs) for u in terms if u is not t):
315:             continue  # a sum of other terms
316:         if not any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(f)}\b", rhs) for f in field_tokens):
317:             F.append(Finding("fieldless_term", "mg5", f"`{t['name']}` contains no field", t["line"]))
318: 
319:     # --- rule 15: declarations -----------------------------------------------
320:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
321:         sc = (_prop(c["body"], "SelfConjugate") or "").strip()
322:         qn = _prop(c["body"], "QuantumNumbers")
323:         if sc == "True" and qn and re.search(r"->\s*-?[1-9]", qn):
324:             F.append(Finding("selfconjugate_with_qn", "warn",
325:                              f"class `{cn}` is SelfConjugate and carries QuantumNumbers {qn}",
326:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {cn}")))
327:         if sc == "True" and _prop(c["body"], "AntiParticleName"):
328:             pass
329:     # Majorana mass normalisation
330:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
331:         if (_prop(c["body"], "SelfConjugate") or "").strip() == "True" and c["head"].startswith("F"):
332:             mm = re.search(r"Mass\s*->\s*\{\s*(\w+)", c["body"])
333:             if not mm:
334:                 continue
335:             M = mm.group(1)
336:             pat = re.compile(rf"(-?\s*(?:1/2|0\.5|\(1/2\))?\s*\*?\s*{M}\b[^;]{{0,40}}{cn}bar\s*\.\s*{cn}\b)")
337:             for t in terms:
338:                 for hit in pat.finditer(t["body"]):
339:                     if not re.search(r"1/2|0\.5", hit.group(1)):
340:                         F.append(Finding("majorana_mass_no_half", "checks",
341:                                          f"`{t['name']}`: Majorana mass term for `{cn}` without the 1/2",
342:                                          t["line"]))
343:     # undeclared symbols in terms (conservative: capitalised identifiers used as fields)
344:     declared = set(class_names) | {c + "bar" for c in class_names} | set(param_names) | \
345:         SM_FIELDS_ALL | SM_PARAMS | SM_MASSES | FR_BUILTINS | set(term_names) | set(index_decls) | \
346:         {"If", "Which", "Table", "KroneckerDelta", "Transpose", "Inverse", "ArcTan", "Sec", "Csc",
347:          "Cot", "Abs", "MatrixExp", "DiagonalMatrix", "IdentityMatrix", "Sum", "Product"}
348:     for c in classes:
349:         for key in ("Mass", "Width"):
350:             v = _prop(c["body"], key) or ""
351:             declared |= set(re.findall(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", v)) - {"Internal", "External", "Automatic"}
352:     for c in classes:
353:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
354:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
355:                 declared |= {mem, mem + "bar"}
356:         for m in re.finditer(r"Unphysical\s*->\s*True", c["body"]):
357:             pass
358:     for t in terms:
359:         b = re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', "", t["body"])
360:         locals_ = set()
361:         for m in re.finditer(r"(?:Block|Module)\[\s*\{([^}]*)\}", b):
362:             locals_ |= {x.strip().split("=")[0].strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",")}
363:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", b):
364:             s = m.group(1)
365:             if s in declared or s in locals_ or s == t["name"] or len(s) < 2:
366:                 continue
367:             if re.match(r"^(mu|nu|rho|sig|la|lam|al|be|sp|ss|ii|jj|kk|ll|ff|gg|cc|aa|bb|tt|rr|xx|yy|zz)\d*$", s):
368:                 continue
369:             if s in ("ExpandIndices", "FlavorExpand", "Index", "Sqrt", "HC"):
370:                 continue
371:             if s[0].isupper() and re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(s)}\s*[\[.]", b):
372:                 F.append(Finding("undeclared_symbol", "warn",
373:                                  f"`{t['name']}` uses `{s}` which is neither declared here nor by SM.fr",
374:                                  t["line"]))

378:     for iname, rng in index_decls.items():
379:         if re.search(r"Range\[\s*6\s*\]", rng) and "AddGaugeRepresentation" not in text:
380:             F.append(Finding("sextet_without_representation", "warn",
381:                              f"index `{iname}` has range 6 but there is no AddGaugeRepresentation", _line_of(text, iname)))

383:     # --- mass mixing written into Definitions (the dominant check failure) ----
384:     phys_new = {cn for cn, c in class_names.items() if (_prop(c["body"], "Unphysical") or "").strip() != "True"}
385:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
386:         d = _prop(c["body"], "Definitions") or ""
387:         if not d:
388:             continue
389:         fields_in = {s for s in re.findall(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", d) if s in phys_new or s in SM_CLASSES}
390:         fields_in -= {cn}
391:         if len(fields_in) >= 2 and re.search(r"\b(sa|ca|sin|cos|Sin|Cos|s\w*|c\w*)\w*\b", d):

## Objective
- Read TASK.md and execute it: extract the complete new-physics content of the SLQrules model (arXiv:2105.04844) into a `spec.json` FeynRulesModel object, run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until schema + lint pass, and end with a self-audit message.
- Work only inside `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-SLQrules-e1vaqirb/`

## Important Details
- TASK.md rules: `model_name` must be `"SLQrules_gen"`; all numeric physics values are STRINGS (`"-1/3"`, `"1500."`); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups []`; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need no `index_decls`; other indices need `index_decls` (`range_kind "NoUnfold"`, correct size); every particle needs a unique `class_index`; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields.
- COMPLETENESS IS SCORED: every new state (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) as a separate ParticleClass entry (or `class_members`); new coupling/mass/mixing params (External unless clearly derived); main new-physics `lagrangian_terms` as verbatim Mathematica strings with FeynRules idioms.
- Rule 6: no cached/reference `.fr` for this model may be opened; confirmed via glob — only `SM.fr` exists (fair game as SM reference).
- Bash DENIED except `./frgen spec.json` (deny-all rule confirmed; `wc` attempt was rejected → use read tool for everything else). Iterate `./frgen`; judge remaining lint findings as harmless and record them in the audit.
- Rule 3 (CC idioms): paper's ψ^c → `CC[psi]`, ψ̄^c → `bar[CC[psi]]`; use class fields with Generation index (e.g. `vl[ff]`), never class members like `ve[nn]`. Paper appendix `sec:appendix` (line 6082, with `sec:CCprescription` 6123, `sec:CCexample` 6140, `sec:CCFeynman` 6219) is about computing Feynman rules from CC fermions, NOT needed for writing the Lagrangian — skipped.
- Rule 4 idioms: `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`; barred+unbarred doublets → shared index; same conjugation type → `Eps[ii, jj]`, never shared.
- NEW physics analysis (settled by charge bookkeeping, corrected d-quark charge Q=−1/3): for `Y1LL (Q̄'^cT iσ2 L') Φ1†`, the SU(2) contraction MUST be the Eps/ε pairing `Q̄^c1 L2 − Q̄^c2 L1` (both components Q=−1/3, neutral with Φ1† +1/3); the shared-index (δ) pairing gives 1 / −4/3 → charge-wrong. Tension with rule 4's literal barred+unbarred→shared guidance remains for `bar[CC[QL]]` vs `LL` — resolve by checking SM.fr's actual index/CC conventions before finalizing L_f terms.
- Rule 11: every new coupling param gets `InteractionOrder {NP,1}` (overrides paper's `{QED,2}` on Y13); `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` must declare all orders, e.g. `{{QCD,1},{QED,2},{NP,1}}`.
- Rule 12: tensor params need explicit per-component `value_rules`; no pattern rules.
- Rule 13: flavour structure as matrix products between class fields (`LLbar.yN.NR` style), never explicit index sums `VCKMR[ff1, ff2] ...`, never nested generation indices.
- Names must not collide with SM.fr (ee, gs, gw, sw, cw, vev, MZ, MW, CKM, Phi, H, Z, W, A, G, cabi, ...) nor FR/Mathematica builtins (FR_SYMBOLS/PROTECTED in fr_lint.py). Safe new names: m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3, Y1, Yt1, Y2, Yt2, Y3, Y22, Yt2t2, Y33, A1t2, At23, Y2t2, Yt13, Y13, Y1RR, Y1LL, Y1QLL, Y1QRR, Yt1RR, Yt1QRR, Y2RL, Y2LR, Yt2RL, Y3LL, Y3QLL.
- Output: ONLY the JSON written to `spec.json`; final message must be the self-audit (Q/Y/SU2/SU3/charge sums per term, mixing-matrix hermiticity, InteractionOrder/ParameterType sweep, particle/parameter/term counts).
- User directive: "Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed."

### Paper physics (authoritative)
- 5 scalar LQ reps, all SU(3) fundamental 3: Φ1 (SU2 1, Y=−1/3), Φ~1 (SU2 1, Y=−4/3), Φ2 (SU2 2, Y=7/6), Φ~2 (SU2 2, Y=1/6), Φ3 (SU2 3, Y=−1/3) (lines 541–572).
- Charge eigenstates: Φ1^−1/3; Φ~1^−4/3; Φ2=(Φ2^+5/3, Φ2^+2/3); Φ~2=(Φ~2^+2/3, Φ~2^−1/3); σ·Φ3 = [[Φ3^−1/3, √2Φ3^+2/3],[√2Φ3^−4/3, −Φ3^−1/3]] ⇒ 9 components (−1/3 ×3, +2/3 ×3, −4/3 ×2, +5/3 ×1).
- L^LQ = L_2Φ + L_kin + L_f + L_3Φ + L_4Φ; W matrices (~706); mass matrices (~725–733) e.g. m1²+v²/2(Y1−|A1t2|²/m²_{t̃21}), mt2²+v²/2(Yt2+|A1t2|²/m²_{t̃21}+|At23|²/m²_{t̃23}), m3²+v²/2(Y3−|At23|²/m²_{t̃23}), m²_ab ≡ m_a²−m_b².
- Covariant derivatives (~855–867): Φ1: ∂+(i/3)g1B−gsλ/2G; Φ~1: ∂+(4i/3)g1B−gsλ/2G; Φ2: ∂−(7i/6)g1B−ig2σ/2W−gsλ/2G; Φ~2: ∂−(i/6)g1B−ig2σ/2W−gsλ/2G; Φ3: ∂+(i/3)g1B−ig2ε̃_I W^I−gsλ/2G.
- L_kin ⊃ i(e/sw cw)Σ_q(Φ^{q†}ℤ^q ↔∂^μ Φ^q)Z_μ + i(e/sw)Σ_{q≠+5/3}((Φ^{q+1})†𝕎_q^{q+1} ↔∂^μΦ^q)W^+_μ; ℤ/𝕎 matrices lines 885–930; charge matrices ~932.
- L_2Φ bracket terms (~700–730): Y1..Y3, Yt1, Yt2, Y22, Yt2t2, Y33 (dim-4, real), A1t2, At23 (dim-1, complex), Y2t2, Yt13, Y13 (dim-0, complex) + masses m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3.
- L_3Φ implementable triples (8): A_1~2~2, A_~12~2, Y_1~12, Y_123, Y_1~23, Y_~123, Y_233, Y_~233.
- L_f Yukawas: Y1RR, Y1LL, Y1Q LL (sym), Y1Q RR, Yt1RR, Yt1Q RR (antisym), Y2RL, Y2LR, Yt2RL, Y3LL, Y3Q LL (antisym); eq:LQ_yukawa ~1017, C matrix eq:Cmatrix ~1035; terms include `Y1RR ū'^c_i ℓ'_j Φ1†`, `Y1LL (Q̄'^cT iσ2 L')_j Φ1†`.
- L_4Φ (~1150–1199): only SM-like quartic Higgs self-coupling structure.
- Paper's FR implementation (Methods): physical `S[100] S1m13hat` (Q=−1/3, colour triplet, Mass Internal), unphysical `S[101] S1m13` (Unphysical→True, Definitions via `W13mat`), param `Y13` External/ComplexParameter/BlockName Y13/Value 1.0/InteractionOrder {QED,2}; all couplings default to unity; Table tab:Lagrangians (lines 1226–1240): LQall, LQ2Phi, LQkin, LQf, LQ3Phi, LQ4Phi; repo https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules (line 1210–1213).
- 9 mass eigenstate names: S1m13hat, S1m43hat, R2p53hat, R2p23hat, R2tm13hat, R2tm23hat, S3m13hat, S3p23hat, S3m43hat.
- Unphysical definition idiom: `S1m13[cc_] :> HC[W13mat[1,1]] S1m13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[2,1]] R2tm13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[3,1]] S3m13hat[cc]`.
- Paper Lagrangian idiom: `L2t33NonHC := Module[{a,b,c,...}, ExpandIndices[ Y2t33 R2t[a,aa] Eps[a,b] 2*Ta[D,b,c] Phi[c] S3[E,bb] I*Eps[D,E,F] S3[F,cc] Eps[aa,bb,cc], FlavorExpand->{SU2D,SU2W}]]; L2t33 := L2t33NonHC + HC[L2t33NonHC];` — field names: `S1`=Φ1, `R1`=Φ~1, `R2`=Φ2, `R2t`=Φ~2, `S3`=Φ3, `Phi`=SM Higgs; coupling naming: `t` suffix after representation number marks tilde (`R2t`=Φ̃2, `Y2t33`=Y_{2̃33}).

### Tooling / lint facts

You are benchmarking automated extraction of a BSM physics model from its paper, to be compared against the physicist's own FeynRules implementation.

MODEL: SLQrules (SimpleExtensions) — FeynRules DB entry based on arXiv:2105.04844.
PAPER: the paper's LaTeX source is the file "paper/2105.04844_source.tex" (read it completely with your file-reading tool; equations, fractions and roots are exact; it is authoritative).
SCHEMA: read tools/frgen/frmodel.py (pydantic FeynRulesModel) before you write the spec.

TASK — extract the COMPLETE new-physics content:
1. Read the paper. Identify EVERY new particle beyond the Standard Model: spin (S/F/V), colour rep (singlet/triplet/sextet/octet), SU(2) rep, electric charge Q and/or hypercharge Y, mass parameter. COMPLETENESS IS SCORED — a model with several new states (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) must include all of them as separate ParticleClass entries (or class_members).
2. Identify the new coupling/mass/mixing parameters (External unless clearly derived).
3. Include the main new-physics lagrangian_terms (verbatim Mathematica strings, FeynRules idioms).

SCHEMA RULES: all numeric physics values are STRINGS ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on => gauge_groups []; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need NO declaration; any OTHER index (e.g. a colour-sextet index, a new-generation index) NEEDS an index_decls entry (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); every particle needs a unique class_index; self_conjugate=false for complex fields (distinct antiparticle), true for real/Majorana fields.

OUTPUT: write the FeynRulesModel JSON object to spec.json in the current directory with your file-writing tool (ONLY the JSON). Set model_name to "SLQrules_gen". Run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate as described under TOOLKIT. Your final message: the self-audit table and one line with the last ./frgen result. spec.json as it is on disk when you stop is rendered and scored.

SANDBOX: the current directory contains ONLY the paper (paper/2105.04844_source.tex), SM.fr (the Standard
Model file this add-on is loaded on top of: take field names, index conventions and
hypercharges from it), the schema tools/frgen/frmodel.py, the renderer
tools/frgen/render.py, the lints tools/fr_lint.py and the command ./frgen. Nothing else
exists here and nothing outside this directory may be read. You have file read, search and
write tools, and ONE shell command: `./frgen spec.json`. No other shell command, no web,
no FeynRules, no Mathematica and no MadGraph.

TOOLKIT: `./frgen spec.json` (1) validates spec.json against the FeynRulesModel schema and
prints every schema error, (2) renders model.fr with the deterministic renderer, and (3)
lints model.fr with deterministic rules, each tagged with the stage it predicts will fail.
Run it after you write spec.json, fix what it reports, and run it again until the schema
is OK and every remaining lint finding is one you have checked and judged harmless.

## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
   - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
   - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
   - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.

4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.

5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
   - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.
   - Otherwise cross-check the placement against a second equation of the paper that depends on the same coefficient (a partial width, a cross section, a limit, or a small-parameter expansion) and name that equation in the self-audit. A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
   - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.
   Never silently pick one placement.

8. Mass mixing. When the paper diagonalises a mass mixing between a new state and an SM state (Z-Z', h-S, W-W_R, nu-N), write the mass eigenstates the paper uses: declare the mixing angle (External, or Internal with the paper's formula) and express the gauge eigenstates through it in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes. Do not leave the mixing in a comment.

## FeynRules and UFO construct rules (each one broke a compile or a MadGraph import in earlier runs)

9. Non-fundamental colour representations. If a field carries a colour index other than the triplet `Colour` or the adjoint `Gluon` (for example a sextet), declare the index range AND add the representation line FeynRules needs, before the field declarations: `AddGaugeRepresentation[SU3C -> {T6, Sextet}];` for a sextet (schema: put both lines in `raw_preamble`; also keep the `index_decls` entry). Write covariant derivatives on the whole field, `DC[Phi, mu]`, never with an explicit colour index inside `DC[...]`.

10. Names. Class names, parameter names and index names must not be Mathematica built-ins or FeynRules symbols: never `N`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `I`, `K`, `O`, `HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, and never a name SM.fr already declares (`H`, `Phi`, `Z`, `W`, `A`, `G`, `ee`, `gs`, `gw`, `sw`, `cw`, `vev`, `MZ`, `MW`, ...). No primes or punctuation in `ParticleName`/`AntiParticleName` (`W'` is not a valid UFO name; write `Wp`, `Wpbar`). Use class indices of 100 or more for new classes.

11. Interaction orders. Every new coupling parameter (Yukawa, portal, quartic, new gauge coupling, dimensionless EFT coefficient) carries an `InteractionOrder`: `{NP, 1}` for a new-physics coupling, `{QED, 1}` or `{QCD, 1}` only when it is literally that coupling. Declare `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` with every order you use (for example `{{QCD, 1}, {QED, 2}, {NP, 1}}`). A coupling with no order makes MadGraph reject the UFO ("Some couplings have '1' order").

12. Tensor parameters. Give every indexed parameter explicit per-component values (`yN[1,1] -> 0.1, yN[1,2] -> 0, ...`; schema: `value_rules`). Never use a pattern rule such as `X[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> ...` in `Definitions`: FeynRules exports the pattern verbatim as a UFO parameter name and MadGraph fails with an unrelated "invalid syntax" error.

13. Flavour structure in matrix form. Write generation-space couplings as matrix products between class fields, `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `LLbar.yN.NR`, `ISbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.IS`, not as explicit index sums `VCKMR[ff1, ff2] uqbar[ff1, cc]...dq[ff2, cc]`, and never nest one generation index inside another. Explicit-index forms leak FeynRules internals (`ConvertSpinToString`, `MakeIdenticalFermions`) into the UFO.

14. One declared total. Define exactly one Lagrangian term named `LTotal` that sums every other term you define, and make sure every other term appears in that sum. Do not define two alternative totals. Do not emit a term that contains no field (a pure constant): FeynRules exports it as a vertex with no particles.

15. Declarations. Every field used in a term is declared; every parameter used in a term is declared with a numeric default; every `SelfConjugate -> True` class has no `QuantumNumbers`; a Majorana mass term is `-1/2 M psibar.psi`.

## Mandatory self-audit table (produce it BEFORE the model)

For every Lagrangian term you emit, output one row of this table. Then fix any row that fails before you write the model.

| term name | fields in the monomial | operator mass dimension d | coupling symbol | coupling mass dimension (must be 4 - d) | 1/Lambda power present (must be d - 4, or "n/a" if d <= 4) | Q sum | Y sum | SU(2) contraction (singlet? which Eps or shared index) | SU(3) contraction | sum of each new U(1) charge (one column per U(1), must be 0) | lepton/baryon number sum (if the paper assigns them) | CC[] used where paper writes psi^c (yes/no/n/a) | fraction/root placement checked against (equation, LaTeX line, or "n/a") | Hermitian partner (HC[] or self-conjugate) |

Rules for the table:
- Field mass dimensions: scalar 1, vector 1, fermion 3/2, `FS[...]` 2, `del`/`DC` 1.
- Every Q sum, Y sum, and new-U(1) sum must equal 0. Use the charges you declared in `QuantumNumbers` and the SM.fr charges for SM fields. If a sum is not 0, the term is wrong; fix the contraction or the charge before you continue.
- If d > 4, the row must show `1/Lambda^(d-4)` and an External cutoff parameter, or a Description that states the absorbed dimension and units.
- Add one row per new particle class that confirms its kinetic + mass term exists and is in the total Lagrangian sum.
- Add one row per non-fundamental colour representation that confirms the `AddGaugeRepresentation[...]` line is present.
- Add one line under the table that lists every `SelfConjugate -> True` class and confirms it carries no `QuantumNumbers`.
- Add one line that lists every class, parameter and index name you chose and confirms none is a Mathematica built-in, a FeynRules symbol, or an SM.fr name.
- Add one line that names the single total Lagrangian and lists the terms it sums.
- Add one line that states whether any reference or cached model file was read (must be "none").

"""

Structured schema for a FeynRules ``.fr`` model file.

This is the shared representation produced by Lagrangian extraction and consumed
by the ``.fr`` generator (render.py). Design principle: STRUCTURE the regular,
error-prone blocks (M$Parameters, M$ClassesDescription, M$GaugeGroups,
M$Information, IndexRange) so an LLM never hand-writes their Mathematica syntax,
and CARRY the irregular parts (Lagrangian algebra, mixing blocks, NLO
bookkeeping) as verbatim Mathematica strings.

All numeric fields are strings so exact FeynRules syntax survives untouched:
rationals like ``-1/3``, decimals like ``1500.``, scientific ``2.5*^-3``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

from pydantic import BaseModel, model_validator

# A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
NumberStr = str


class Rule(BaseModel):
    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""

    lhs: str
    rhs: str
    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"

    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"


class ParamType(str, Enum):
    External = "External"
    Internal = "Internal"


class SpinType(str, Enum):
    S = "S"  # scalar
    F = "F"  # fermion
    V = "V"  # vector
    U = "U"  # ghost
    T = "T"  # tensor
    W = "W"  # Weyl fermion
    R = "R"  # spin-3/2
    RW = "RW"


class RangeKind(str, Enum):
    Unfold = "Unfold"
    NoUnfold = "NoUnfold"
    Range = "Range"


class PropType(str, Enum):
    Sine = "Sine"
    Straight = "Straight"
    ScalarDash = "ScalarDash"
    GhostDash = "GhostDash"
    Curly = "Curly"
    W = "W"
    C = "C"
    S = "S"
    D = "D"


class PropArrow(str, Enum):
    true = "True"
    false = "False"
    none = "None"
    forward = "Forward"


class ModelInfo(BaseModel):
    authors: List[str]
    version: str
    date: str
    institutions: List[str] = []
    emails: List[str] = []


class GaugeGroup(BaseModel):
    """A M$GaugeGroups entry. Omitted entirely by BSM add-on models."""

    name: str  # LHS symbol: U1Y, SU2L, SU3C
    abelian: bool
    gauge_boson: str
    coupling_constant: Optional[str] = None
    charge: Optional[str] = None  # required iff abelian
    structure_constant: Optional[str] = None  # required iff non-abelian
    symmetric_tensor: Optional[str] = None
    representations: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # [("T","Colour")] or many
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM rule strings

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "GaugeGroup":
        if self.abelian and not self.charge:
            raise ValueError(f"gauge group {self.name}: Abelian group needs charge")
        if not self.abelian and not self.structure_constant:
            raise ValueError(
                f"gauge group {self.name}: non-Abelian group needs structure_constant"
            )
        return self


class IndexDecl(BaseModel):
    name: str  # Colour, Generation, SU2W ...
    range_kind: RangeKind
    size: int  # Range[size]
    style_symbol: Optional[str] = None  # IndexStyle[name, style_symbol]


class Parameter(BaseModel):
    """A M$Parameters entry (LHS symbol of ``==``)."""

    name: str
    parameter_type: Optional[ParamType] = None
    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # scalar; tensors use value_rules
    value_rules: List[Rule] = []  # tensor Value -> { ... }
    complex: Optional[bool] = None  # ComplexParameter
    block_name: Optional[str] = None  # External only
    order_block: Optional[int] = None  # External SCALAR only
    interaction_order: Optional[Tuple[str, int]] = None  # -> {NP, 1}
    indices: List[str] = []  # non-empty => tensor
    definitions: List[Rule] = []
    parameter_name: Optional[str] = None
    tex: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    tensor_class: Optional[str] = None
    # tensor-only flags
    unitary: Optional[bool] = None
    hermitian: Optional[bool] = None
    orthogonal: Optional[bool] = None
    allow_summation: Optional[bool] = None

    @property
    def is_tensor(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.indices)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "Parameter":
        if self.is_tensor:
            if self.value is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: tensor uses value_rules, not scalar value"
                )
            if self.order_block is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: order_block forbidden on tensors"
                )
        exclusive = [f for f in (self.unitary, self.hermitian, self.orthogonal) if f]
        if len(exclusive) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: at most one of unitary/hermitian/orthogonal"
            )
        if (self.unitary or self.hermitian) and self.complex is False:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: unitary/hermitian require complex=True"
            )
        if self.orthogonal and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(f"parameter {self.name}: orthogonal must be real")
        if self.parameter_type == ParamType.External and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: External params must be real "
                "(split into real/imag or make Internal)"
            )
        return self


class MassSpec(BaseModel):
    """Renders 0 | {sym} | {sym,val} | {sym,Internal} | {gen,{m1,v1},...}."""

    massless: bool = False  # -> literal 0
    sym: Optional[str] = None
    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # number | "Internal" | "Automatic" | None
    members: List[Tuple[str, Optional[NumberStr]]] = []  # multi-gen

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "MassSpec":
        if not self.massless and not self.sym:
            raise ValueError("MassSpec needs massless=True or a sym")
        return self


class ParticleClass(BaseModel):
    """A M$ClassesDescription entry, e.g. ``S[100] == {...}``."""

    spin_type: SpinType
    class_index: int  # the n in S[100]
    class_name: str
    self_conjugate: bool
    indices: List[str] = []  # -> Index[...] wrapped
    flavor_index: Optional[str] = None  # BARE name
    class_members: List[str] = []
    mass: Optional[MassSpec] = None
    width: Optional[MassSpec] = None
    quantum_numbers: Dict[str, NumberStr] = {}  # values are strings -> preserve -1/3
    pdg: Optional[Union[int, List[int]]] = None
    particle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    antiparticle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    full_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_label: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_type: Optional[PropType] = None
    propagator_arrow: Optional[PropArrow] = None
    unphysical: bool = False
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM Mathematica rule strings
    ghost: Optional[str] = None  # U[n] only
    goldstone: Optional[str] = None  # S[n] only
    weyl_components: List[str] = []
    majorana_phase: Optional[str] = None
    chirality: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def class_label(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.spin_type.value}[{self.class_index}]"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "ParticleClass":
        if self.unphysical:
            if self.mass or self.pdg:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields omit mass/pdg"
                )
            if not self.definitions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields require definitions"
                )
        if len(self.class_members) > 1:
            if not self.flavor_index:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: multi-member class needs flavor_index"
                )
            n = len(self.class_members)
            for lst in (
                self.pdg,
                self.particle_name,
                self.antiparticle_name,
                self.full_name,
            ):
                if isinstance(lst, list) and len(lst) != n:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"particle {self.class_name}: list length must equal "
                        f"member count ({n})"
                    )
        if self.spin_type == SpinType.U:
            if self.self_conjugate:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: ghosts must be self_conjugate=False"
                )
            if not self.ghost:
                raise ValueError(f"particle {self.class_name}: ghost needs ghost=<boson>")
        return self


class LagrangianTerm(BaseModel):
    name: str  # LHS symbol
    expression: str  # VERBATIM Mathematica RHS
    delayed: bool = False  # True -> ":=", False -> "="


def _references(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    """True if ``name`` appears in ``text`` as a whole Mathematica token."""
    if not text:
        return False
    return re.search(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9$]){re.escape(name)}(?![A-Za-z0-9$])", text) is not None


def _param_refs(p: Parameter, names: set) -> set:
    """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
    texts: List[str] = []
    if p.value:
        texts.append(p.value)
    for r in p.value_rules:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    for r in p.definitions:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    blob = " ".join(texts)
    return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}


def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
    """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.

    Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
    dependency cycle.
    """
    names = {p.name for p in params}
    deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
    by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}

    ordered: List[Parameter] = []
    emitted: set = set()
    remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order

    while remaining:
        progressed = False
        still: List[str] = []
        for n in remaining:
            if deps[n] <= emitted:
                ordered.append(by_name[n])
                emitted.add(n)
                progressed = True
            else:
                still.append(n)
        remaining = still
        if not progressed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
            )
    return ordered


class FeynRulesModel(BaseModel):
    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""

    model_name: str
    info: ModelInfo
    interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")

        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
        builtin = {
            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
        }
        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
        return self

351:         op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
352:         # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
353:         # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
354:         # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
355:         rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
356:         for lead in (":=", "="):
357:             if rhs.startswith(lead):
358:                 rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359:                 break
360:         sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")
361: 
362:     env = Environment(
363:         loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364:         autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),
365:         keep_trailing_newline=True,
366:     )
367:     template = env.get_template("model.fr.j2")
368:     return template.render(model_name=model.model_name, body="\n\n".join(sections))

## Objective
- Read TASK.md and execute it: extract the complete new-physics content of the SLQrules model (arXiv:2105.04844) into a `spec.json` FeynRulesModel object, run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until schema + lint pass, and end with a self-audit message.
- Work only inside `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-SLQrules-e1vaqirb/`

## Important Details
- TASK.md rules: `model_name` must be `"SLQrules_gen"`; all numeric physics values are STRINGS (`"-1/3"`, `"1500."`); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups []`; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need no `index_decls`; other indices need `index_decls` (`range_kind "NoUnfold"`, correct size); every particle needs a unique `class_index`; `self_conjugate=false` for complex fields.
- COMPLETENESS IS SCORED: every new state as a separate ParticleClass entry (or `class_members`); new coupling/mass/mixing params (External unless clearly derived); main new-physics `lagrangian_terms` as verbatim Mathematica strings with FeynRules idioms.
- Rule 1: free-field kinetic+mass term for EVERY new particle class using the class's `Mass -> {M, value}` symbol, included in the total sum. Rule 14: exactly ONE root term `LTotal` summing all others; no fieldless/constant terms. Rule 15: every param used in a term declared with numeric default. Final message = self-audit (tables: one row per Lagrangian term w/ Q/Y/SU2/SU3 charge sums, one row per new particle class confirming kinetic+mass term + presence in total, one line naming the total and its summed terms; plus mixing-matrix hermiticity, InteractionOrder/ParameterType sweep, particle/parameter/term counts).
- Bash DENIED except `./frgen` / `./frgen *` (deny-all rule with explicit allows confirmed again this session — a `grep` bash call was rejected); use read/grep tools for everything else. `./frgen` is the only allowed command.
- Rule 3 (CC idioms): ψ^c → `CC[psi]`, ψ̄^c → `bar[CC[psi]]`; class fields with Generation index, never class members like `ve[nn]`. Paper appendix (line 6082+) decided NOT needed.
- Rule 4 idioms: `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`; barred+unbarred doublets → shared index; same conjugation type → `Eps[ii, jj]`, never shared.
- Charge bookkeeping (re-verified this session): `Y1LL (Q̄'^cT iσ2 L') Φ1†` MUST use Eps pairing `Q̄^c1 L2 − Q̄^c2 L1` (comp1: +2/3 −1 +1/3 = 0; comp2: −1/3 +0 +1/3 = 0, both neutral); shared-index pairing is charge-wrong (1 / −4/3). iσ2 = [[0,1],[−1,0]] gives exactly the Eps contraction. Eps used despite rule 4's literal barred+unbarred→shared hint (document in audit).
- Rule 11: every new coupling param gets `InteractionOrder {NP,1}`; hierarchy must include NP, e.g. `{{QCD,1},{QED,2},{NP,1}}`.
- Rule 12: tensor params need explicit per-component `value_rules`; no pattern rules (pattern rules ⇒ mg5 finding).
- Rule 13: flavour as matrix products between class fields (`LLbar.yN.NR`, `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`), never `M[ff1, ff2] fieldbar[...]` explicit sums, never nested generation indices.
- Names must not collide with SM.fr or FR/Mathematica builtins (FR_SYMBOLS/PROTECTED in fr_lint.py). SM classes confirmed: A, Z, W, G, ghA, ghZ, ghWp, ghWm, ghG, B, Wi, ghB, ghWi, vl/{ve,vm,vt}, l/{e,mu,ta}, uq/{u,c,t}, dq/{d,s,b}, LL, lR, QL, uR, dR, H, G0, GP, Phi. Safe new names: S1, R1, R2, R2t, S3 (multiplets), 9 `...hat` eigenstates, m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3, Y1, Yt1, Y2, Yt2, Y3, Y22, Yt2t2, Y33, A1t2, At23, Y2t2, Yt13, Y13, Y1RR, Y1LL, Y1QLL, Y1QRR, Yt1RR, Yt1QRR, Y2RL, Y2LR, Yt2RL, Y3LL, Y3QLL. Avoid SM params: ee, gs, gw, g1, sw, cw, vev, MZ, MW, MH, yl, yu, yd, lam, CKM, muH, cabi, ...
- External + ComplexParameter True is FORBIDDEN by frmodel.py ("External params must be real"); complex couplings must be Internal+complex or External-real (schema wins over paper). Mass-basis choice still open (see Active).

### fr_lint.py exact mechanics (derived this session)
- `term_defs`: starts `^(L\w+)\s*:?=`; block ends at next `M$\w+ =`, `L\w+ :?=`, or `\w+ = {`; param `X == {` does NOT terminate a term (verified regex backtracking).
- Rule 11 (missing_interaction_order): fires only if term has used params AND none of them carries InteractionOrder AND body lacks SM coupling words (ee/gw/gs/g1/yl/yu/yd/lam/CKM) AND lacks `DC[`/`FS[`; `_is_kin_name` (name contains "kin"/"gauge") skips the check entirely. Strategy: all new couplings get orders; free-field terms contain `DC[` or are kin-named; pure mass terms folded into kin-named or mixed terms.
- `mixing_in_definitions`: fires when class Definitions reference ≥2 other physical/SM classes AND regex `\b(sa|ca|sin|cos|Sin|Cos|s\w*|c\w*)\w*\b` matches text ⇒ colour dummy in Definitions must be `aa` (NOT `cc`); `HC[W13mat[...]]`, `mat`, capital-S names are safe (no word starts lowercase s/c).
- `explicit_flavour_sum`: `\b(\w+)\[\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|ii\d?)\s*,\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|jj\d?)\s*\]\s*\w+bar\[` with group(1) ∈ OUR file's `param_names` — e.g. `yd[ff2, ff3] QLbar[` would fire if `yd` declared in our file; SM-style explicit-gen form is also condemned by task rule 13 ⇒ use matrix products.
- `nested_generation_index`: `Index[Generation, x], Index[Generation` or `X[Generation, x]` — avoid.
- `explicit_index_in_dc`: no explicit index inside `DC[Field[idx], ...]`.
- Undeclared-symbol check: capital letter followed by `[` or `.` must be in `declared`; `declared` includes Mass/Width spec tokens (so mass symbols used in terms are safe even if absent from M$Parameters). `CC`, `bar`, `Eps` are in FR_BUILTINS.
- `is_mass` (line ~231) is dead code — unused.
- One root (`LTotal`); every term must contain a field name or be a sum of other terms; `SelfConjugate True` ⇒ no nonzero QuantumNumbers; low_class_index warns if < 100 (use 100+); no `$` in names; particle names must not contain `'`, backtick, whitespace, ``!@#%^&*()=[]{}|\;:<>?/,``.

### Paper physics (authoritative)
- 5 scalar LQ reps, all SU(3) triplet: Φ1 (SU2 1, Y=−1/3), Φ~1 (SU2 1, Y=−4/3), Φ2 (SU2 2, Y=7/6), Φ~2 (SU2 2, Y=1/6), Φ3 (SU2 3, Y=−1/3) (lines 541–572).
- Charge eigenstates: Φ1^−1/3; Φ~1^−4/3; Φ2=(+5/3,+2/3); Φ~2=(+2/3,−1/3); σ·Φ3 ⇒ 9 components (−1/3 ×3, +2/3 ×3, −4/3 ×2, +5/3 ×1).
- L^LQ = L_2Φ + L_kin + L_f + L_3Φ + L_4Φ; W matrices (~706); mass matrices (~725–733) e.g. m1²+v²/2(Y1−|A1t2|²/m²_{t̃21}), mt2²+v²/2(Yt2+|A1t2|²/m²_{t̃21}+|At23|²/m²_{t̃23}), m3²+v²/2(Y3−|At23|²/m²_{t̃23}); m²_ab ≡ m_a²−m_b².
- Covariant derivatives (~855–867); L_kin Z/W derivative couplings (~885–930).
- L_2Φ (~700–730): Y1..Y3, Yt1, Yt2, Y22, Yt2t2, Y33 (dim-4, real), A1t2, At23 (dim-1, complex), Y2t2, Yt13, Y13 (dim-0, complex) + masses m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3.
- L_3Φ implementable triples (8): A_1~2~2, A_~12~2, Y_1~12, Y_123, Y_1~23, Y_~123, Y_233, Y_~233.
- L_f (lines 993–1015, read this session): Y_a^{AB} 3×3 complex LQ–quark–lepton matrices; Y_a^{Q,AA} quark–quark; symmetries: Y1QLL symmetric, Y~1QRR and Y3QLL antisymmetric, Y1QRR arbitrary; colour indices omitted when trivial. Terms: `Y1RR ū'^c_i ℓ'_j Φ1†`, `Y1LL (Q̄'^cT iσ2 L')_j Φ1†`, `Y1QLL (Q̄'^cT_{c1} iσ2 Q'_{c2}) Φ_{1,c3} ε^{c1c2c3}` (colour ε!), `Y1QRR ū'^c_{c1} d'_{c2} Φ_{1,c3} ε`, then Φ~1 terms (line 1007+) etc.; `+ h.c.` each; eq:LQ_yukawa ~1017, C-matrix eq:Cmatrix ~1035.
- L_4Φ (~1150–1199): SM-like Higgs quartic only.
- Paper FR implementation: physical `S[100] S1m13hat` (Q=−1/3, triplet, Mass Internal), unphysical `S[101] S1m13` (Unphysical→True, Definitions via `W13mat`), param `Y13` External/Complex/BlockName Y13/Value 1.0/InteractionOrder {QED,2}; all couplings default unity; 9 eigenstate names: S1m13hat, S1m43hat, R2p53hat, R2p23hat, R2tm13hat, R2tm23hat, S3m13hat, S3p23hat, S3m43hat; unphysical idiom `S1m13[cc_] :> HC[W13mat[1,1]] S1m13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[2,1]] R2tm13hat[cc] + HC[W13mat[3,1]] S3m13hat[cc]` (QuantumNumbers → {Y -> −1/3}, Indices → {Index[Colour]}) — our version must use colour dummy `aa` instead of `cc`; Lagrangian idiom `Module[{a,b,c,...}, ExpandIndices[..., FlavorExpand->{...}]] + HC[...]`; field names S1=Φ1, R1=Φ~1, R2=Φ2, R2t=Φ~2, S3=Φ3, Phi=SM Higgs; `t` suffix after representation number marks tilde (Y2t33 = Y_{2̃33}).
- Lagrangian variable names (tab:Lagrangians, lines 1226–1240): LQall, LQ2Phi, LQkin, LQf, LQ3Phi, LQ4Phi; repo https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules (line 1210).

### Design decisions (settled)
- **Design M**: 9 physical hat classes (`Mass -> {sym, Internal}`) + 5 unphysical gauge multiplets with W-matrix `definitions` (covers "multiplets, mass eigenstates" completeness wording).
- Complex couplings can't be External+complex ⇒ leaning External-real `"1."` defaults with tensor Yukawas as External `value_rules` (diagonal unity); Internal+complex alternative noted for audit.
- Lint-avoidance tactics: kin-named free-field terms (`...kin`) containing `DC[`/`FS[` to skip rule 11; colour dummy `aa` in Definitions; no explicit generation indices anywhere; matrix-product flavour form.
- Double-counting analysis (rule-1 tension, UNRESOLVED): (A) hat free terms with Internal masses + gauge-basis bare-mass terms −m1²|S1|² double count after W-substitution; (B) hat free terms only ⇒ m1..m3 never enter L (Internal masses wrong at v=0); (C) gauge-basis masses only ⇒ hat classes lack mandated free-field rows; possible resolution: write bare masses on gauge basis + hat free terms kinetic-only, or check paper's field listing (lines ~1330–1410) whether unphysical classes carry Mass. Must be settled before writing spec.json.
